# AI-DLC Documentation

AI-DLC is a structured, gated methodology for AI-driven software development.
This repository runs it natively in Claude Code, Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, Codex CLI,
Cursor, opencode, and GitHub Copilot.
## Quick Start

### 1. Install

macOS, Linux, or WSL:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```

The native installer sets up everything AI-DLC needs, every harness runtime
included; you do not need to install Bun or Node.js. On Windows, it installs for
the current account and automatically
registers the bin directory in User PATH; run it from a normal PowerShell window,
since one opened with "Run as administrator" gets a warning and a prompt. A
terminal app or IDE that was already open keeps its old PATH, so quit and reopen
it before using `aidlc` there; a new tab inside it is not enough. Use
[`-NoModifyPath`](guide/18-install-and-lifecycle.md#windows-powershell) to skip
both persistent and current-process PATH changes.

### 2. Configure

Run from your project root:

```bash
aidlc config --harness claude
aidlc doctor
```

Replace `claude` with `kiro`, `kiro-ide`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, or
`copilot`. A bare `aidlc config` starts the interactive setup.

### 3. Start

Open the configured harness and describe the work:

```text
/aidlc Build a REST API for inventory management
```

Codex CLI uses `$aidlc`. See [Getting Started](guide/01-getting-started.md) for
provider setup, trust prompts, project refreshes, and the first workflow.

# aidlc-workflows release highlights

This guide summarizes selected improvements from the upstream CHANGELOG. [All releases](changelog.md) includes the complete entries, with fixes and upgrade instructions, from the bundled source revision.

## 2.11.1

[2.11.1, released October 20, 2026](releases/2.11.1.md), retains State Version 8 and the 33-stage base graph.

Code kept in a git worktree, a clone, a submodule or a monorepo package now reaches Code Generation's approval question; where the review cannot see the code, the question says `AI-DLC found no source changes under <where it looked>` once and the person approves as usual. With Guard Policy off, a build carries on after the chat compacts. Going back from the open Code Generation gate goes through on the first ask. A person who pauses in their own words is not pushed on, and a park names the way back. The plan question waits for the person's reply before work starts, and a plan of two or more Units asks once who builds them (Just me, or Several teams).

Plugins someone else builds carry their author's own names (`<name>@<catalogue>`); AI-DLC's own plugins share one `aidlc-plugins` catalogue that stays put across updates, and plugins compose without Bun on Cursor and Kiro IDE. A project on any release from 2.8.0 refreshes without stopping. AI-DLC's status line is the person's choice, asked once. `install.sh` and `aidlc uninstall` take an opt-in `--allow-root`, and a project's `.env` no longer reaches the engine.

Run `aidlc update`, then `aidlc config --yes` per project; open work carries on. Copy users replace the complete `runtime/<harness>/` tree from `aidlc-copy-runtime-2.11.1.tar.gz`. Plugin users in Claude Code or Codex add AI-DLC's plugin catalogue once with `/plugin marketplace add <folder>` or `codex plugin marketplace add <folder>`. Scripts that build or install plugins AI-DLC does not ship must use `<name>@<catalogue>` instead of `aidlc-<name>@aidlc-plugins`.

## 2.11.0

[2.11.0, released October 8, 2026](releases/2.11.0.md), retains State Version 8 and the 33-stage base graph.

New work starts leaner: outside `enterprise`, Guard Policy is off and the new `collaborators` setting is off, so each stage runs with its lead agent only (`/aidlc --collaborators on` brings the support agents back). The engine asks for Plan Approval and asks about an approved plan once; `express` and `poc` ship with it off. Replies are read in the person's own words from any chat, a bare `/aidlc` carries on with open work, and requests such as `--skip`, `--add`, a scope change or a Construction setting are done at once with the way back. Finished Units stay finished across those changes. A composed plan belongs to its piece of work and writes no scope file unless saved.

`aidlc config` now runs beside open work and keeps the team's own files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, `opencode.json`, and one `.gitignore` block after the team's rules). A tool whose hooks never run stops at the first message with its own setup step. On Windows, `install.ps1` in a UAC-elevated window warns and asks instead of refusing.

Run `aidlc update`, then `aidlc config --yes` per project; open work carries on. Copy users replace the complete `runtime/<harness>/` tree from `aidlc-copy-runtime-2.11.0.tar.gz`, which needs Bun 1.3.8 or newer.

## 2.10.0

[2.10.0, released September 24, 2026](releases/2.10.0.md), retains State Version 8 and the 33-stage base graph.

Eligible new solo workflows use serial, unit-major Construction with verified Unit checkpoints. Verification uses the recorded, human-authorized command; existing workflows retain their recorded policy. Parallel execution uses explicit stage-major/swarm settings and verified batch checkpoints.

Guard Policy replaces Change Control and supports strict, relaxed and off. Human approval gates and Unit ownership remain mandatory. Legacy names remain readable for this release. Non-colliding harnesses can coexist, share neutral onboarding, and keep the current provider unless Bedrock is selected. Intent-scoped Bolt worktrees avoid name collisions; parked attempts restore exact bytes and Doctor shows recovery commands.

Refresh between workflows. Run `aidlc update`, then `aidlc config --yes` and `aidlc doctor` per project. Refresh each installed harness with `aidlc config --harness <name> --yes`. Copy users replace the complete `runtime/<harness>/` tree from `aidlc-copy-runtime-2.10.0.tar.gz`.

## 2.9.0

[2.9.0, released September 15, 2026](releases/2.9.0.md), keeps State Version **8** and the **33-stage** base graph. New Classic intents use 18 stages through Build and Test. Existing Classic intents keep their recorded graph; use `workshop` for the prior 26-stage route (`--test-strategy standard` restores the Standard test floor).

| Change | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Classic v1 ceremony | One human approval per stage; advisory reviews, sensors and learnings on, skeleton and summary confirmation off |
| Atomic intent settings | Apply depth, testing, review, change control and three ceremony switches together; invalid values reject the whole command |
| Intent archive | Retire unfinished work without deleting its record, then unarchive when needed |
| Commit provenance | Attribute committed paths to reviewed Units, classify drift and missing evidence, and report the trust basis |
| On-demand autonomy | Grant or revoke Construction autonomy while preserving the first approval, Unit Plan Approval and failure stops |
| Install and models | Separate Bun copy assets; no provider question on Kiro; balanced effort is medium for all three groups |
| Review retries | Use the current ordinal after rejection to avoid false budget-exhaustion stops |

## 2.8.2

[2.8.2, released September 10, 2026](releases/2.8.2.md), fixes summary confirmations, review-findings diagnostics, and Unit lifecycle handling. It includes the native installation and hook fixes in [2.8.1](releases/2.8.1.md). State Version remains 8, with 33 stages.

| Release | Improvement | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [2.8.2](releases/2.8.2.md) | Summary confirmation tolerates a decorative divider before Assumption Confirmation | Appending the section no longer invalidates an unchanged confirmed summary; substantive edits still require confirmation |
| [2.8.2](releases/2.8.2.md) | Malformed review-findings rows report their cell count and expected columns | Missing or surplus cells can be corrected without guessing which column was omitted; malformed rows still block review completion |
| [2.8.2](releases/2.8.2.md) | Wave stages reject serial Unit start, pause, and resume | The engine preserves state and audit and directs callers to `unit complete --wave`; switching back to unit-major leaves remaining units completable |
| [2.8.1](releases/2.8.1.md) | Fix native setup defaults, same-version updates, and Cursor/Copilot hook routing | Enter accepts setup defaults, current installs pass integrity checks under normal umasks, and native hook adapters receive the right arguments and emit valid Cursor allow responses |

The [2.8.6 entry](releases/2.8.6.md) is retained upstream as superseded development history. No 2.8.6 release was published; 2.8.2 was the intended release at that time. The current bundled target is 2.11.1.

## 2.8.0

[2.8.0, released September 8, 2026](releases/2.8.0.md), consolidates the 2.7.x cycle. Runtime behavior is unchanged from 2.7.2. State Version remains 8, with 33 stages.

| Release | Improvement | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [2.8.0](releases/2.8.0.md) | New minor baseline for the 2.7.x fixes | Version output and release archives use 2.8.0; existing 2.7.2 records need no migration |
| [2.7.2](releases/2.7.2.md) | Tag-bound release identity and versioned runtime archives | Installers check source identity and SHA-256, with signed attestation verification when a compatible GitHub CLI is available |
| [2.7.1](releases/2.7.1.md) | Fix solo Plan Approval deadlock | The Stop hook's read-only probe no longer invalidates approval, allowing Code Generation to begin |

## Upgrading

Run `aidlc update`, then `aidlc config --yes` in each project and `aidlc doctor`. To pin the release, use `install.sh --version 2.9.0` or `install.ps1 -Version 2.9.0`. Manual-copy users replace the complete `runtime/<harness>/` tree from `aidlc-copy-runtime-2.9.0.tar.gz` and use Bun. Migrate scripts from the removed standalone `aidlc-utility.ts change-control` route to `aidlc engine config set change-control <strict|relaxed>`. Unknown `config-change` flags now fail. Pre-2.9 reviews remain `unverifiable` for commit provenance until their next Unit review writes committed evidence. See the [2.9.0 entry](releases/2.9.0.md) and [installation guide](guide/18-install-and-lifecycle.md).

# aidlc-workflows 0.1.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.1.0] - 2026-04-24

Initial public release.

* `/aidlc` orchestrator skill with 5 phases (Initialization, Ideation, Inception, Construction, Operation) and 32 stages
* 11 domain-expert agents: product, design, delivery, architect, aws-platform, compliance, devsecops, developer, quality, pipeline-deploy, operations — invoked by the orchestrator based on stage and scope
* 9 adaptive scopes (enterprise, feature, mvp, poc, bugfix, refactor, infra, security-patch, workshop) that route through different stage subsets
* `--depth` flag with three levels (minimal, standard, comprehensive) to control process rigor per stage
* `--test-strategy` flag with three levels (Nyquist Minimal, Standard, Comprehensive) independent of depth — workshop scope defaults to Minimal
* `--stage`, `--phase`, `--scope` jump flags for moving directly into a specific point in the workflow
* `--status`, `--doctor`, `--help`, `--init`, `--test-run` utility handlers
* Bolt-by-Bolt Construction: dependency DAG execution with walking skeleton mode, autonomy mode, and per-bolt quality gates
* Stage protocol with approval gates at every stage, structured question format, and session resume from any checkpoint
* TypeScript hooks for audit logging (37-event taxonomy), state preservation, statusline sync, and session recovery — runs natively on Windows without Bash
* `AWS_AIDLC_DEFAULT_SCOPE` environment variable so organizations can pin a default scope at the shell or profile level
* Statusline showing current phase, stage, agent, model, and context usage with phase-scoped progress
* Three-tier test suite (smoke, unit, feature, integration) with LLM-behavioral tests via `--test-run`
* `BOLT_*` audit event taxonomy for Construction phase tracking
* Two-tier documentation: User Guide (`docs/guide/`) and Developer Reference (`docs/reference/`)
* Promoted 7 agents (architect, compliance, devsecops, developer, quality, pipeline-deploy, operations) to Opus; shipped Bedrock model IDs as defaults
* Pinned orchestrator to Opus with 1M context on Bedrock
* `/aidlc --help` documents all CLI utilities and flags with examples
* Windows compatibility: hooks and the statusline ported from Bash to TypeScript; `--doctor` is platform-aware; no jq or Bash prerequisites
* macOS compatibility across the test suite (BSD vs GNU utilities, whitespace padding, AppleDouble sidecar files)

# aidlc-workflows 0.2.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-05-03

Breaking release. State file format is now v5 and cannot be migrated from v4 — in-flight workflows must be restarted:

    mv aidlc-docs aidlc-docs-v4-archive && /aidlc --init --force --scope <scope>

* Workflow `Status` values simplified to `Running` and `Completed`. Replaces `In Progress`, `Paused`, and `Waiting for Approval` — pause has no UX and approval waits moved to the stage level (see next bullet)
* Two new stage states: `[?]` means the stage is waiting for your approval, `[R]` means you rejected the gate and it's being revised. Previously both situations looked like `[-]` and you couldn't tell them apart from `--status`
* `/aidlc --status` now tells you who the blocker is. When a stage is `[?]`: "Awaiting your approval on <stage>". When `[R]`: "Revising <stage> (revision N of 3)". Previously always read "Running" even when the workflow was waiting on you
* `/aidlc --doctor` gains a drift check — catches the rare case where the audit log records a workflow completion but the state file disagrees
* `/aidlc --init` is now one fast deterministic call (under a second). Replaces the previous multi-tool-call flow that sometimes hit timeouts
* `--force` flag on `/aidlc --init` — rewrites `aidlc-state.md` and warns about any unrelated artifacts found in `aidlc-docs/`. Without `--force`, re-running init on an existing workflow exits with a helpful message instead of hanging
* Approving a stage now advances the workflow atomically. The approval flips the gate, marks the stage complete, and moves you to the next stage in one step. Fixes the previous failure mode where `/aidlc --status` could show "Awaiting your approval" after you'd already approved
* Compaction-aware resume. If your Claude Code context is compacted during a stage, resuming surfaces a three-option prompt (continue / review prior artifact / restart stage) instead of silently picking up stale context
* `--test-run` early stops emit `WORKFLOW_COMPLETED` with `Reason=test-run-stopped-at-<target>` so CI harnesses get a clean terminal state to assert on
* `--scope <x>` can be used mid-workflow to change scope in place. The stage plan re-derives and skipped stages flip to `[S]` if the new scope excludes them
* Welcome message now renders at session start via `settings.json` `companyAnnouncements` instead of running as a workflow stage. Total stage count dropped from 32 to 31
* Statusline progress bar now tracks the current phase. Previously the bar was workflow-scoped (e.g. 15/31) while the numeric ratio was phase-scoped (e.g. 5/7), so the bar could appear stuck for multiple stage advances
* Invalid `AWS_AIDLC_DEFAULT_SCOPE` values now error cleanly and exit without creating state. Previously could hang or ask clarifying questions in non-interactive mode
* New reference documentation chapter at `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md` covering the workflow, phase, and stage state machines, the audit event taxonomy, and the same-commit doc/code consistency rule
* Canonical state file schema is documented as State Version 5. Audit log consumers that parse free-form markdown headings (`## Artifact Update`, `## Subagent Completed`) must switch to the `**Event**:` field shape — these sections are no longer emitted
* Audit event taxonomy rebalanced: 5 auto-event types removed (test-run selections now tag canonical events with `Test-Run: true`), session lifecycle events now emitted by hooks (SessionStart / SessionEnd / PreCompact), artifact lifecycle events now emitted by the PostToolUse hook. Taxonomy: 47 → 41 events, each with a tool-owned emitter

# aidlc-workflows 0.3.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.3.0] - 2026-05-15

Foundation release. v0.3.0 reshapes how stages, scopes, agents, and artifacts are defined so later releases can ship Construction worktrees, three-compartment stages, sensors, the Ralph loop driver, the fitness compiler, and the visual workflow designer without rewriting plumbing. By design no new user-facing workflows — your v0.2.0 workflows run the same way. State file format bumps from v5 to v6 with no field changes; in-flight workflows archive-and-reinit:

    mv aidlc-docs aidlc-docs-v5-archive && /aidlc --init --force --scope <scope>

* **BREAKING for CI and shell automation**: `/aidlc --doctor` now exits non-zero when any check fails (previously always exited 0). Any CI job or `set -e` shell script that invoked doctor and continued on will now abort. Restore the old behaviour with `|| true`

# aidlc-workflows 0.3.10

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.3.10] - 2026-05-19

Adds `audit-fork` and `audit-merge` subcommands to `aidlc-audit.ts`, completing the audit half of the per-Bolt fork/merge primitive (alongside worktree create/merge and state fork/merge). Both subcommands follow audit-of-intent semantics extended from the `WORKTREE_*` events: `AUDIT_FORKED` and `AUDIT_MERGED` emit to the main audit *before* the disk operation, so a kill-9 between emit and disk surfaces as a phantom audit row reconciled by `--doctor`. The worktree audit is byte-for-byte self-contained at fork instant — its copy includes the `AUDIT_FORKED` entry by virtue of the emit-then-copy order. Delta detection at merge is parse-driven (locate the AUDIT_FORKED block in the worktree audit, take everything after its closing separator); the `Fork Boundary` field on AUDIT_FORKED anchors a SHA-256 prefix-hash sanity check that refuses to merge if main audit's prefix has been tampered with mid-Bolt. Solo Bolts as of this patch — no SKILL.md call sites yet (wired in a later release).

* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-audit.ts audit-fork --slug <slug>` emits `AUDIT_FORKED` to the main audit, then mkdirs `<worktree>/aidlc-docs/` and copies the main audit byte-for-byte to the worktree. The `Fork Boundary` field records the byte offset of the main audit immediately BEFORE the AUDIT_FORKED row landed; `Source Audit Hash` records SHA-256 of those same prefix bytes. The worktree's copy of the AUDIT_FORKED row carries the same fields, so audit-merge can recover them without inspecting main
* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-audit.ts audit-merge --slug <slug>` reads the worktree audit's most recent AUDIT_FORKED entry for the slug, recomputes main audit's prefix-hash at byte `Fork Boundary` and refuses with `prefix-hash` error if it disagrees with the recorded `Source Audit Hash`. On success, locates the byte position immediately after the AUDIT_FORKED block's closing `\n---\n`, appends the post-fork delta to main, and emits `AUDIT_MERGED` (with `Entries Merged`, `Source Audit Hash`, `Fork Boundary`) to the main audit only. Lock budget extended from 5s default to 20s (`acquireAuditLock(projectDir, 200, 100)`) to absorb N=4-8 Bolt-merge contention
* All `aidlc-audit audit-fork` / `audit-merge` failures route through `appendAuditEntry("ERROR_LOGGED", ...)` with `[slug=<slug>]` for `--doctor` correlation; post-emit failures additionally tag the message with `[fork-emitted:<timestamp>]` so doctor can distinguish "intent recorded, disk operation never landed" from earlier failure modes
* `audit-format.md:127-128` and `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md:283-284` Emitter cells for `AUDIT_FORKED` / `AUDIT_MERGED` now point at `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-audit.ts`. Required Fields cells updated to include `Fork Boundary` and the per-event extra fields
* `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md` § "Audit-of-intent exception" renamed to § "Audit-of-intent semantics" — the pattern now covers 5 events (3 `WORKTREE_*` + 2 `AUDIT_*`). `STATE_FORKED` / `STATE_MERGED` deliberately stay under the strict audit-first invariant — state writes are idempotent where `git worktree add` is not, so a failed state write surfaces as recoverable drift instead of an unrecoverable orphan. The 2-row event-group/emitter/disk-op table documents only the audit-of-intent half; STATE_* lives under the strict-first section above
* New worktree-tier test `tests/worktree/t07-audit-fork-merge.sh` (31 assertions across three phases): smoke (fork creates byte-identical worktree audit; AUDIT_FORKED in both audits with matching Fork Boundary; merge appends delta; AUDIT_MERGED in main only), edge cases (empty delta; missing aidlc-docs subdir auto-created; missing main audit fails loud; prefix-hash mismatch refusal; N=2 lock contention via 50ms stagger; lock-timeout failure path with planted stuck lock; 65-char slug rejected with length error; post-emit failure ERROR_LOGGED carries `[fork-emitted:<iso-ts>]` for doctor correlation), and property (N=4 alphabetical / reverse-alphabetical / same-second-timestamps / one-empty-delta scenarios all preserve per-Bolt fork→merge bracket order in the merged main audit)
* `BOLT_SLUG_REGEX` and `validateBoltSlug(slug)` exported from `lib.ts` — centralises the kebab-case Bolt slug regex (was previously duplicated as `SLUG_RE` in `aidlc-worktree.ts` and `SLUG_REGEX` in `aidlc-audit.ts`). Adds 64-char max-length check so pathologically long slugs fail fast with a clear error instead of surfacing as cryptic mkdir/copy failures. `aidlc-audit.ts` adopts the helper now; `aidlc-worktree.ts` keeps its tool-local `SLUG_RE`
* `AIDLC_AUDIT_LOCK_RETRIES` and `AIDLC_AUDIT_LOCK_RETRY_MS` env-var overrides for `audit-merge`'s lock budget — defaults stay at `200 × 100ms = 20s` for parallel-Bolt contention; tests dial these down so the lock-timeout failure path runs in ~100ms instead of 20s. Lock-timeout error message now reports the actual budget exhausted (`Failed to acquire audit lock after N × Mms = X.Xs retries; another merge in flight?`)
* `audit-merge` prefix-hash mismatch error now distinguishes truncation from mid-prefix mutation: when `mainBuf.length < boundary`, the error reads "expected at least N bytes, got M" so doctor can surface the right failure mode
* `appendAuditEntryUnlocked` is adopted on both the happy and error paths of `audit-merge` so the delta-append + AUDIT_MERGED emit (happy) and the delta-append + ERROR_LOGGED emit (catch) each run inside a single locked critical section, with no release-and-reacquire across either boundary

## [0.3.11] - 2026-05-19

`aidlc-bolt.ts` worktree subcommands — the per-Bolt lifecycle integration on top of the `aidlc-worktree` primitive, state fork/merge, and audit fork/merge. Three new flag-driven branches mirror the lifecycle's three terminal states: `start --worktree` (delegates to `aidlc-state fork` + `aidlc-audit audit-fork`), `complete --merge` (delegates to `aidlc-state merge` + `aidlc-audit audit-merge`), `abort [--discard]` (third terminal verb, optional worktree tear-down). Atomicity follows the shipped `handleSetAutonomy` precedent: validate inputs FIRST, emit primary audit event AFTER validation, THEN delegate to the state/audit subprocess CLIs which emit their own events inside `withAuditLock`. Failures emit a `BOLT_FAILED` recovery row plus a `{ok:false, slug, stage, reason, detail}` envelope for halt-and-ask consumption. SKILL.md per-Bolt loop is updated to use the new flags as single-call lifecycle boundaries (replaces the separate Step 0.6 / Step 6.8 prose with `aidlc-bolt --worktree`/`--merge` invocations that own the audit + delegate ordering). The three pre-registered `MERGE_DISPATCH_*` events get their emitter wiring at SKILL.md Steps 0 and 6.5 via `bun aidlc-audit.ts append --event MERGE_DISPATCH_* ...` — no new tool code, no new audit registration.

* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-bolt.ts start --name "<bolt-names>" --batch <n> [--walking-skeleton true|false] [--worktree --slug <kebab-slug>]` — `--worktree` requires `--slug`, rejects csv `--name`. After BOLT_STARTED, spawns `aidlc-state.ts fork --slug <slug>` (emits STATE_FORKED, registers slug in main's Bolt Refs, byte-copies state to `<worktreePath>/aidlc-docs/aidlc-state.md`) then `aidlc-audit.ts audit-fork --slug <slug>` (emits AUDIT_FORKED audit-of-intent, byte-copies main audit). Audit order: `BOLT_STARTED → STATE_FORKED → AUDIT_FORKED`
* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-bolt.ts complete --name "<bolt-names>" --batch <n> [--merge --slug <kebab-slug>]` — `--merge` requires `--slug`, rejects csv `--name`. After BOLT_COMPLETED, spawns `aidlc-state.ts merge --slug <slug>` (emits STATE_MERGED, removes slug from Bolt Refs, applies per-field merge rule from worktree state) then `aidlc-audit.ts audit-merge --slug <slug>` (emits AUDIT_MERGED, appends post-fork delta from worktree audit). AIDLC metadata consolidates BEFORE SKILL.md Step 6.5's git-merge dispatch
* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-bolt.ts abort --name "<name>" --slug "<slug>" --reason "<text>" [--discard]` — third terminal verb. Emits BOLT_FAILED with `Reason: aborted` (sub-classifier; no new event type, audit count stays at 55). Default preserves the worktree directory for inspection. With `--discard`, spawns `aidlc-worktree.ts discard --slug <slug>` (audit-of-intent emits WORKTREE_DISCARDED before tear-down) and reports `discarded: true` in the JSON response
* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-bolt.ts fail` gains optional `--slug <kebab-slug>` for halt-and-ask correlation — `aidlc-worktree info --slug` reads the most-recent WORKTREE_CREATED entry and joins on the slug field downstream
* All three new flag branches print a `{ok: false, slug, stage: "start-worktree"|"complete-merge"|"abort-discard", reason, detail}` envelope on stdout when sub-step delegation fails. Distinct from `aidlc-worktree merge`'s `{status: "conflict", conflict_files, ...}` envelope so halt-and-ask can render different prompts. Subprocess timeouts at 30s match the merge-dispatch budget; on SIGTERM the reason is `*-timeout` rather than `*-failed`
* SKILL.md Construction Flow per-Bolt loop refactored: Step 1 now invokes `aidlc-bolt start --worktree --slug <slug>` as a single tool call replacing the previous Step 0.6 (state-fork) + Step 1 (BOLT_STARTED) split. Step 6 now invokes `aidlc-bolt complete --merge --slug <slug>` replacing the previous Step 6 + Step 6.8 split. Steps 0.6 / 6.8 prose removed (delegation now lives inside `aidlc-bolt`)
* `MERGE_DISPATCH_INVOKED` / `_RETURNED` / `_FALLBACK` events at `audit-format.md:147-149` stay Reserved — emitter assignment deferred. Reason: SKILL.md prose telling the LLM to call `aidlc-audit.ts append` for these events would violate the t48 "no prose audit emission" invariant the project enforces (the LLM under `claude -p` can hallucinate permission policies on prose-directed tool calls; the documented fix is to route emission through a dedicated tool subcommand). A later change owns the per-Bolt orchestrator rewrite and will absorb dispatch instrumentation via a new `aidlc-bolt dispatch-event` (or equivalent) subcommand. Audit count stays at 55 — events were pre-registered, no new registration needed
* `abort --discard` now spawns `aidlc-worktree discard` BEFORE emitting `BOLT_FAILED` (was the reverse). Reason: emit-then-discard left audit + reality divergent on discard timeout — audit said "aborted" while the worktree still existed on disk and the slug remained in main's Bolt Refs. Default-path (no `--discard`) ordering unchanged
* `audit-format.md:113` and `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md:236` BOLT_FAILED rows updated to document the new optional fields (`Bolt slug`, `Reason: aborted`) and the new emitter (`tools/aidlc-bolt.ts abort` alongside `fail`)
* New `tests/unit/t77-bolt-worktree-flags.sh` (28 assertions) — pins atomicity ordering, complete 5-field envelope shape (`ok`, `slug`, `stage`, `reason`, non-empty `detail`), abort sub-classifier, default-abort worktree directory preservation, regression guards on existing no-flag paths

The three `WORKTREE_*` events follow audit-of-intent semantics — emit fires before `git`, and `doctor` reconciles disk vs audit drift if a kill-9 / OS-crash interrupts the operation between those points. **Constraint:** `aidlc-worktree` must run from the main repo checkout, not from a sibling worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`. The Construction orchestrator's per-Bolt loop in `SKILL.md` now includes Step 0 (worktree create dispatch + verify) and Step 6.5 (worktree merge dispatch + verify); the verify backstop is what makes the agent dispatch deterministic without prose-grepping audit.md.

* `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-worktree.ts create --slug <slug> --base <branch>` adds a per-Bolt worktree at `.aidlc/worktrees/bolt-<slug>` on a new `bolt-<slug>` branch, emits `WORKTREE_CREATED` audit event before invoking git

Construction worktrees + split-safe state/audit + practices discovery. Construction Bolts now execute in their own git worktree at `.aidlc/worktrees/bolt-<slug>/`, eliminating race conditions on shared state, audit, and working tree across parallel Bolt batches and workshop scenarios. State and audit fork to the worktree on Bolt start and merge back on gate approval, with deterministic conflict resolution.

A new Inception stage `practices-discovery` at slot 2.2 captures team branching strategy, walking-skeleton stance, testing posture, deployment, and code style — affirmed once per project, then read by Construction so worktree dispatch and walking-skeleton sequencing reflect the team's voice rather than scope-hardcoded defaults. State template bumps from v6 to v7 with three real field additions; v6 workspaces archive-and-reinit:

    mv aidlc-docs aidlc-docs-v6-archive && /aidlc --init --force --scope <scope>

Halt-and-ask AUQs render the worktree path and branch name verbatim
* **New Inception stage `practices-discovery` at slot 2.2** — discovers team branching strategy, walking-skeleton stance, testing posture, deployment patterns, and code style from evidence (brownfield: multi-agent scan of git, configs, code, and reverse-engineering artifacts) or `AskUserQuestion` (greenfield); affirmation gate promotes drafts to `.claude/practices/team.md` and `.claude/rules/aidlc/guardrails/project-guardrails.md`. The `info` JSON envelope returns `{slug, path, branch_name, audit_timestamp, merge_held}` — the `merge_held` field powers the multi-failure HOLD-MERGE invariant during halt-and-ask

## [0.4.10] - 2026-05-29

The headline learning gate: a new `aidlc-learnings.ts` tool implementing the §13 Learnings Ritual as tool-as-actor (replaces the prior LLM-as-actor §13 prose; the "steering loop" is renamed to the "learning loop" throughout). Between a gated stage's completion verification and its approval, the orchestrator runs `aidlc-learnings.ts surface --slug <slug>`; the tool reads the stage's `memory.md` (via the new `parseMemoryEntries` helper), surfaces each non-blank entry under Interpretations / Deviations / Tradeoffs verbatim as a candidate plus a read-only "parked open questions" list, and emits a structured JSON candidate set. The orchestrator renders AskUserQuestion; the user ticks candidates to keep and may type free-text additions, picking which of the four headings each belongs under — **the heading pick is the user's only classification, and the destination is derived from it, not picked.** Before any write, the orchestrator runs a single-line section-level admission conflict check against `aidlc-org.md`'s matching section; a contradicting entry is rejected with the org sentence quoted inline and the user revises, skips, or escalates (no override path). Conflict-clear selections are persisted via `aidlc-learnings.ts persist`, which writes dated rolling entries to the two-surface `.claude/rules/aidlc-project-learnings.md` (default) and `aidlc-team-learnings.md` files — a separate surface from the practices files, never `## Corrections` and never the practices-discovery topical sections. A one-click "promote scope" affordance widens a candidate from project to team; there is no org-learnings file and no widen-to-org path. All writes go through one `withAuditLock` with a decide-inside-lock transaction and content-presence idempotency (a `<!-- cid:<slug>:<id> -->` marker per written line) so a crashed run recovers without double-appending. Audit count grows 61 → **63**: `RULE_LEARNED` and `SENSOR_PROPOSED`.

When a learning is a sensor-binding addition, the same locked transaction does the pull-authoring two-write install: it scaffolds a project-tier `<project>/.claude/sensors/aidlc-<id>.md` manifest (with a `matches:` capability glob) AND atomically appends the new id to the originating stage's `sensors:` frontmatter list. The sensor binds and fires from the next workflow's compile — the never-edits-stage-files rule is lifted for sensor-binding frontmatter edits only (the immutable `## Steps` / `## Sensors` / `## Learn` body is untouched; stage files are now framework-and-loop-edited, documented in CLAUDE.md). `SENSOR_PROPOSED` records the manifest path, the bound stage(s) (`Destinations`), and `source: orchestrator | user_addition`.

This also closes the `runtime-graph.json sensor_firings[]` work carried since the runtime-graph compile shipped: `aidlc-runtime.ts compile()` now walks `SENSOR_FIRED` / `SENSOR_PASSED` / `SENSOR_FAILED` / `SENSOR_BUDGET_OVERRIDE` rows in each stage's window, pairs by 8-hex `fire_id` correlator (positional pairing breaks under the 4-sensors-per-Write fan-out), and populates `sensor_firings[]` on every `RuntimeStage` and `BoltInstance`. Orphan FIRED rows are `result: "incomplete"` — immediately in a closed stage window, or after a deterministic 60s cutoff (computed from the max audit timestamp, no wall-clock) in an open window. The same compile pass wires `learnings_captured.{from_orchestrator, from_user_addition}` from the new audit rows (the previously reserved slot). `SensorFiring` gains `fire_id` and widens `result` to `passed | failed | budget-override | incomplete`.

Skipped in TEST_RUN_MODE: the gate ritual surfaces no candidates and persists nothing.

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.4.11] - 2026-05-29

Closes the management-plane half of the control/data-plane redesign. `/aidlc --doctor` gains two new advisory rows that observe rule/sensor state without changing how rules concatenate at runtime. No new flags — doctor stays single-purpose; both rows render quietly when there's nothing to surface. No new audit event types: this wires the emitter for the reserved `GUARDRAIL_LOADED` event, so the v0.5.0 audit count stays at 63.

* `/aidlc --doctor` now reports **Rule drift**: it surfaces team/project (and team/project-learnings) rule files whose `##` headings overlap a populated heading in `aidlc-org.md`, quoting the org sentence inline so you can review for contradiction. The row is advisory — it never fails the health check or blocks a workflow. The semantic contradiction verdict is the orchestrator's at observation time, not doctor's; doctor surfaces the candidate, you (or the orchestrator) judge it.
* `/aidlc --doctor` now reports **Paired sensor coverage**: `Paired sensor coverage: P/(M-X) guardrails paired (X feedforward-only)`, where the denominator counts guardrails that need a sensor (M-X) and the numerator counts those whose named sensor resolves (P). For each rule carrying `pairing: <sensor-id>`, doctor asserts the named sensor exists in at least one stage's resolved sensor set; `pairing: feedforward-only` rules count separately. This is a file-existence check, not a semantic one — it confirms the binding resolves, not that the sensor fits the rule.
* The doctor paired-coverage row now emits the reserved `GUARDRAIL_LOADED` audit event when it resolves the guardrail set. No new event type; the audit registry count is unchanged.

No action needed on upgrade. If you script against `/aidlc --doctor` exit codes, note both new rows are advisory and never change the exit status.

## [0.4.13] - 2026-05-30

Makes the documentation surface public-GitHub-ready and integrates the shipped v0.5.0 chapters into a coherent book. The docs are now split by reader into three guides — a **User Guide** (build software with AIDLC), a new **Harness Engineer Guide** (reshape how AIDLC behaves through configuration — stages, agents, scopes, rules, sensors, knowledge — without writing code), and the **Developer Reference** (change the AIDLC codebase itself). The Developer Reference is renumbered along conceptual dependency — Plane Architecture moves to the front as the lens, Sensor and Rule chapters sit paired after the agent/hook mechanics, and Runtime Graph follows the State Machine. The stability-policy chapter folds its rename=major/addition=minor rule into the artifact-vocabulary chapter. The User Guide gains v0.5.0 coverage: the Rules and the Learning Loop chapter (with a worked example), user-facing Sensors, the three new CLI tools, a planes orientation, and the runtime-graph artifact. The README header is rewritten and now links all three guides. The first time a Sensor fires in a workspace, a one-line banner points you at the loop chapter. A per-page coherence pass across all three guides reconciled the docs with the shipped v0.5.0 code — agent support matrices, hook counts, stage-count and audit-event totals, the §13 Learnings Ritual / Phase Boundary Verification split, sensor `matches` and prefix semantics, and the scope/stage tables now match the graph and tools. The dead guardrail-learning subsystem is retired in the same pass (audit taxonomy drops to 61 events). No upgrade action required.

* The first time a Sensor fires in a workspace, the `aidlc-sensor-fire` hook prints a one-line first-fire banner (pointing at the Rules and the Learning Loop guide chapter) and drops a `.first-fired` marker so it shows once, not on every fire.
* `docs/reference/` chapters are renumbered: Plane Architecture is now `02`, Sensor System `07`, Rule System `08`, Runtime Graph `13`; `09-testing.md` and `12-state-machine.md` keep their numbers. If you bookmarked reference chapters by number, re-check the links.
* `docs/guide/08-guardrails.md` is renamed to `docs/guide/08-rules-and-the-learning-loop.md` and rewritten for the v0.5.0 strict-additive rule model (org → team → project → phase → stage). The dead `org-guardrails.md` / `project-guardrails.md` / `overrides:` / `enforcement:` model is gone from the guide.
* New `docs/harness-engineering/` **Harness Engineer Guide** (8 chapters) documents reshaping AIDLC through configuration rather than code — anatomy of a stage (surfacing the stage-definition schema), adding a stage, adding an agent, scopes, rules and the learning loop, sensors, and team knowledge. Each chapter links down to the authoritative Developer Reference chapter. The `docs/guide/12-customization.md` "Extending AI-DLC" section now points into this guide, and the README Documentation table lists all three reader guides.
* The stability-policy chapter (`docs/reference/15-stability-policy.md`) is removed; all cross-references are updated.

If you grepped audit logs for `GUARDRAIL_TRIGGERED` / `GUARDRAIL_LEARNED`, those rows are no longer emitted.

If your Bedrock region isn't `us-east-1`, override `AWS_REGION` in `.claude/settings.local.json` (the example file gains a commented `AWS_REGION`/`AWS_PROFILE` pair). Getting Started gains a full **AWS Bedrock Setup** section (model-access form, IAM policy, credential options, region override, and the `claude` sign-in wizard), linking the AWS quick-setup guide. Install instructions switched to Claude Code's native installer (`curl … claude.ai/install.sh | bash` / `irm … claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex`), with separate Windows PowerShell and CMD blocks.

# aidlc-workflows 0.4.4

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.4.4] - 2026-05-25

Ships the rule-resolution half of the control-plane substrate. `aidlc-graph compile` now walks `.claude/rules/`, resolves the strict-additive chain (org → team → project → phase, where the phase rule's `paths:` glob matches the stage's synthesised artefact path), and bakes a per-stage `rules_in_context` array into every node of `data/stage-graph.json`. Strict-additive runtime: every applicable rule appears in the chain; nothing drops; the `enforcement:` and `overrides:` keywords are removed from the schema. Conflicts (narrower contradicting broader policy) are rejected at admission gates (practices-discovery, memory gate) by section-level LLM check — not at runtime. Compile now runs under `withAuditLock` with atomic temp-rename writes (`writeFileAtomic`); concurrent invocations serialise and crash mid-write leaves consumers reading the previous compile, never a half-written file. Filename regex permits future `aidlc-{team,project}-learnings.md` surfaces. The compile-output schema change drives the version bump; `data/stage-graph.json` grows about 25% (~+6KB on the 32-stage graph).

* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-rule-schema.ts` (new) — sibling of `aidlc-stage-schema.ts`. Parses and validates rule frontmatter (`paths:` string list + `pairing:` scalar — `feedforward-only` or `aidlc-<sensor-id>` shape). Strips a leading UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) before matching the `^---\r?\n` anchor — macOS/Windows editors occasionally save markdown with a BOM; without stripping, the file would parse as frontmatter-less and silently drop `paths:` and `pairing:`. Tolerates unknown keys for forward-compat; throws `<file>: <message>` on schema violations.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-graph.ts` — `RuleResolution` and `GraphStage.rules_in_context` interface fields; new `loadRules()` walker (anchored filename regex, deterministic `(scope-priority, filename)` sort, `AIDLC_RULES_DIR` env-seam for fixture isolation); new `resolveRulesForStage()` strict-additive chain builder; zero-dep `**`/`*` glob matcher synthesising `aidlc-docs/<phase>/<slug>/` from each stage. `FIELD_ORDER` extends with `rules_in_context` after `outputs`. `compile` write site wraps in `withAuditLock` + `writeFileAtomic`.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-lib.ts` — `listField` and `scalarField` promoted from file-private to exported (rule-schema reuses the zero-dep YAML primitives). New `writeFileAtomic(path, data)` helper — temp + POSIX rename, with cleanup of the temp on write failure. `withAuditLock` is now reentrant within a single process for the same `projectDir` — nested calls bump a depth counter rather than self-deadlocking on the OS-level lock (the prior behaviour burned the 5-second mkdir retry budget before throwing). Cross-process locking is unchanged. The signature is also tightened to forbid `async` callbacks (`fn: () => T extends Promise<unknown> ? never : T`) so a future caller can't pass a Promise-returning function and have the lock release before the work settles.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/data/stage-graph.json` — regenerated. Every stage node grows `rules_in_context`; lengths are 3 (org+team+project) on Initialization stages and Construction stages whose synthesised path doesn't match the phase rule's globs, 4 (org+team+project+phase) elsewhere.
* `tests/fixtures/designer-export/export.json` — regenerated. `aidlc-graph export` propagates `rules_in_context` through `.stages[]`; the byte-equal pin in `t66:879` would otherwise drift.
* `tests/feature/t88-compile-rules-in-context.sh` (new) — 16 TAP assertions across 9 fixture sub-directories under `tests/fixtures/v05-mr7a-rule-resolution/` (org-only, org-team-project, phase-paths-match, phase-paths-no-match, phase-no-paths, all-four, pairing-feedforward-only, zero-rules, bom-frontmatter); covers `--check` drift detection on rule-file edits, round-trip determinism, glob-anchor regression (prefix-only globs don't match concrete paths), schema rejection of invalid `pairing` values, and BOM-prefixed frontmatter parsing.
* `tests/feature/t66-graph-library.sh` — eight new cases (74 → 82 tests): `loadGraph()` carries `rules_in_context` as array; `FIELD_ORDER` places it after `outputs`; canonical-emitter pin proves the field populates from `AIDLC_RULES_DIR`; `compile --check` detects rule-file drift via the env-seam; round-trip stability; concurrency wrap (parallel compiles serialise to a byte-equal serial result); `withAuditLock` reentrancy regression guard (nested same-pd is fast and holds the lock throughout outer scope); exit-handler deregistration regression guard (sequential calls don't accumulate listeners).
* `docs/reference/17-rule-system.md` — chain block at `:42` rewritten from six items to five-layer (`org → team → project → phase → stage`); `enforcement: enforced` and `overrides:` sections deleted in favour of strict-additive runtime + admission-time conflict-rejection prose.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — Rules bullet rewritten: drops the `enforcement: enforced` + `overrides:` sentence; states the five-layer chain and the strict-additive runtime model directly.

## [0.4.5] - 2026-05-25

Both halves of the control-plane substrate now flip to pull authoring: each stage explicitly imports its sensors via a `sensors:` field in frontmatter, and the rule resolver's `paths:` glob mechanism on phase rules disappears in favour of the stage's existing `phase:` field as the pull import for its matching phase rule. Both halves now mirror how stages already declare `consumes`, `requires_stage`, `produces` — frontmatter declares; the resolver looks up. Org/team/project rules continue to attach to every stage automatically by filename. There is now one authoring direction across all stage relationships: stage frontmatter is the single source of truth for what fires when this stage runs.

`aidlc-graph compile` now also walks `.claude/sensors/`, indexes manifests by id, looks up each stage's imports, and bakes a per-stage `sensors_applicable` array into every node of `data/stage-graph.json`. Manifest schema simplifies: `applies_to:` is gone (scope lives on the stage side); `matches` moves to a top-level capability filter consumed by the PostToolUse hook at fire time. The rule resolver's glob machinery (`globToRegex`, synthesised concrete-path matching) deletes entirely.

The 32 stage YAML files gain explicit `sensors:` import lists. The `## Sensors` body compartments are rewritten from "bulleted inventory" to per-stage prose — naming what the stage produces, what each imported sensor checks on those outputs, what failure looks like. The list-of-sensors duplication goes (frontmatter owns that); the per-stage narrative stays. Stage YAML files become framework-and-loop-edited: the learning-loop ritual will append new sensor ids to a stage's `sensors:` list during the gate, where push authoring would have just edited a manifest. Stage files were never strictly framework-immutable on disk; pull authoring makes the edit boundary honest. Every stage node now carries the full resolved control-plane view that the dispatcher and PostToolUse hook read directly.

# aidlc-workflows 0.4.6

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.4.6] - 2026-05-27

Ships the data-plane substrate for the steering loop: a per-workflow `runtime-graph.json` accumulator that fires deterministically on every approval gate. `runtime-graph.json` is the data-plane mirror of `stage-graph.json`, populated by walking `audit.md` + per-stage `memory.md` files. Three downstream consumers now have a stable surface to read from: the gate ritual (silent-diary-skip detection via `memory_entries` count), the doctor (diary-discipline metric via `MEMORY_EMPTY` rows), and v0.10.0's cross-workflow observer (pattern detection across many runs).

The compile is hook-driven, never LLM-tool-coupled. A new PostToolUse hook on the `Bash` matcher fires on every `bun aidlc-(state|jump|bolt|utility).ts` invocation that appends a transition-class audit row (`GATE_APPROVED | STAGE_STARTED | AUDIT_MERGED | WORKFLOW_COMPLETED`); the orchestrator's actual subprocess invocation is the deterministic anchor, regardless of what the LLM does next. `WORKFLOW_COMPLETED` is in the transition set so the final-stage approve fires the compile (otherwise `handleCompleteWorkflow`'s 5-row emit would never record the final stage as approved). v0.4.0-backfill: stages without a `memory.md` file get `memory_entries: null` and emit no `MEMORY_EMPTY` row, distinguishing "never tracked" from "tracked and empty" so v0.4.x users don't see an audit storm on first post-upgrade workflow.

# aidlc-workflows 0.4.7

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.4.7] - 2026-05-27

Ships the first emitter of the four `SENSOR_*` audit events pre-registered earlier. The `aidlc-sensor.ts` dispatcher CLI is a thin routing surface (Q4/Q5): it looks up a manifest by id, generates an 8-hex Fire id correlator, emits `SENSOR_FIRED` under one `withAuditLock`, spawns the per-sensor script (no lock held), and emits the paired terminal row (`SENSOR_PASSED` | `SENSOR_FAILED` | `SENSOR_BUDGET_OVERRIDE`) under a second `withAuditLock`. Two lock windows split across the spawn solve the spawn-window starvation that one-lock-across-spawn would create — long-running sensors (60s tsc) no longer pin the audit lock during their work.

Four framework sensors become real tool calls via their own scripts (`aidlc-sensor-required-sections.ts`, `aidlc-sensor-upstream-coverage.ts`, `aidlc-sensor-linter.ts`, `aidlc-sensor-type-check.ts`). Pull authoring at the manifest level: each manifest's `command:` declares HOW the sensor runs; the dispatcher routes; the per-sensor script does the work. Forks adding custom sensors write a manifest plus a script — no framework-code change.

**Three known limitations are documented forward:**

* **`sensor_firings[]` population deferred.** `aidlc-runtime.ts:319` continues to hardcode `sensor_firings: []` on every compiled `RuntimeStage`. This release emits the audit rows for the four `SENSOR_*` events; a later gate ritual is the first consumer that walks `audit.md` since each stage's `started_at` to populate the array. That consumer must also tolerate orphan FIRED rows (FIRED with no terminal pair, e.g., from a process crash between lock window A and lock window B); pair them as `result: "incomplete"` rather than discarding the FIRED. The current `SensorFiring.result` enum is `"passed" | "failed"`; a later release extends it to cover the four audit-emit terminals: `"passed" | "failed" | "budget-override" | "incomplete"`. The `SensorFiring` interface also gains a `fire_id: string` field so audit-walking can pair by Fire id (load-bearing under the parallel 4-sensors-per-Write fan-out — terminal rows interleave by spawn duration, not by FIRED order; positional pairing breaks). The dispatcher emits `Fire id` on every row.
* **Lock-orphan recovery covers `process.exit()` paths only.** The on-exit handler installed by `withAuditLock` reaps the lock dir on Node's normal exit (including `process.exit()`). SIGKILL — and external SIGTERM with no signal handler — does NOT trigger Node's exit event; the lock dir survives, and the next fire burns the 5s mkdir-EEXIST retry budget before throwing. There is no mtime-based lock-reap in `aidlc-lib.ts` today. Mtime-reap deferred to v0.6.0.
* **Type-check sensor attributes diagnostics to the file tsc reports, not the file that introduced the regression.** The wrapper post-filters tsc's whole-project output to errors whose `file` field equals or contains `--file-path`. Cross-file regressions (e.g., a removed export breaking the consumer) report against the consumer file in tsc's output, not against the file that triggered the change. The sensor emits PASS for `<path>` while the consumer file shows the error; the regression surfaces only when the consumer is later edited and re-fired against. Multi-file attribution model deferred to v0.6.0+.
* **Audit event taxonomy is closed by design.** `aidlc-audit.ts` carries a closed `VALID_EVENT_TYPES` Set (61 events) and throws on unknown types. Forks adding custom sensors plug into the existing four `SENSOR_*` event slots (FIRED, PASSED, FAILED, BUDGET_OVERRIDE); fork-defined event names (e.g., `SENSOR_BENCHMARK_REGRESSED`) are NOT v0.5.0 scope. The closure is intentional: open-ended event names break audit grep regexes, doctor-row counts, downstream parser determinism, and the t28 audit-event-sync drift gate. Pull authoring at the manifest/stage level (forks add their own manifest + script and import via `sensors:`) is fully supported within the closed taxonomy. Custom-event-name extensibility revisited in v0.6.0+ if fork pressure surfaces.

* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor.ts` (new) — dispatcher CLI. Subcommands: `list`, `describe <id>`, `fire <id> --stage <slug> --output-path <path>`. Validates inputs + resolves graph + generates Fire id pre-lock (so a malformed stage file fails validation and exits 1 without ever opening a lock — orphan-FIRED prevention). Truth table for outcome decision (branch-a-precedes-branch-0 ordering: timeout-SIGTERM → BUDGET_OVERRIDE before true-spawn-failure → script-error). Detail-file path keyed on Fire id makes collisions a 1-in-4-billion event by construction; `wx`-flag write + `renameSync` retained as defence-in-depth. CLI exits non-zero only on dispatcher invocation errors; sensor outcomes are advisory and always emit a paired terminal row. Subprocess primitive is `node:child_process spawnSync` (matches `aidlc-bolt.ts:84` precedent — Bun's sync return shape doesn't expose `signal === "SIGTERM"` cleanly).
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-required-sections.ts` (new) — counts distinct `^## ` headings (dedupe by exact text); pass = (count ≥ 2). Stdout JSON carries `pass`, `h2_count`, `headings`, and `findings_count` (the script computes `max(0, 2 - h2_count)` itself; dispatcher reads the field generically). Dispatcher is sensor-id-agnostic for findings derivation — adding a new framework sensor in v0.6.0 doesn't require a switch arm in the dispatcher.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-upstream-coverage.ts` (new) — case-insensitive word-boundary check for each artifact in `--consumes`, accepting either `\b<slug>\b` literal or `[[<slug>]]` wikilink form. Pass = every consumed artifact appears at least once. `--consumes` empty or absent collapses to `pass=true reason="no upstream"`.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-linter.ts` (new) — wraps `bunx eslint --format json --max-warnings=-1`. Probes config via `bunx eslint --print-config <path>`; on no-config or eslint-unavailable, exits 127 (dispatcher → PASSED Note=tool-unavailable per branch b). `pass = errorCount === 0` only — warnings DO NOT FAIL (real configs ship `no-unused-vars: warn`; warning-as-failure would spam SENSOR_FAILED on every Write under the fan-out).
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-type-check.ts` (new) — wraps `bunx tsc --project <tsconfig> --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile <under aidlc-docs/.aidlc-sensors/> --noEmit --pretty false`. `--project` honours the project's actual settings (bare-file `tsc foo.ts` ignores tsconfig and falls back to ES3 defaults — checked-but-meaningless on any real project). Continuation lines (indented related-info) appended to the previous error's `message` rather than dropped (Findings count would otherwise under-report).
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/sensors/aidlc-{linter,required-sections,type-check,upstream-coverage}.md` — `command:` rewritten to point at the per-sensor script (e.g., `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-sensor-linter.ts`). The dispatcher reads the manifest, extracts the .ts basename, and resolves it sibling-style to itself (mirrors `aidlc-bolt.ts:84`).
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/knowledge/aidlc-shared/audit-format.md` — four SENSOR_* Emitter cells flipped from `Reserved` to `` `tools/aidlc-sensor.ts` `fire` ``. Required Fields columns extended with `Fire id` correlator + `Output path`; `SENSOR_FAILED` row's detail-path string updated `aidlc-docs/.sensors/<stage>/<sensor>-<iso>.md` → `aidlc-docs/.aidlc-sensors/<stage>/<sensor>-<fire-id>.md`. Optional `Note` field on `SENSOR_PASSED` documented in a footnote (`tool-unavailable` | `script-error: <reason>`).
* `docs/reference/12-state-machine.md` — same four cell flips at lines 313-316 with backticked path-token format (t48's forward-check regex). Detail-path string updated `<iso>` → `<fire-id>`.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.gitignore` — `aidlc-docs/.aidlc-sensors/` added to runtime-files block.

## [0.4.8] - 2026-05-27

Lands the headline data-plane integration: a `Write|Edit` PostToolUse hook (`aidlc-sensor-fire.ts`) that reads the compile-resolved `sensors_applicable` array off the active stage's `stage-graph.json` node and spawns the dispatcher per matching `matches:` glob. Authoring direction is invisible past compile — the hook reads a list regardless of how the resolver populated it ("the dispatcher does no resolution walks at runtime. Stage entry reads `sensors_applicable` off the node — already looked up, already attached."). After this release ships, customers using AIDLC for actual TS/JS coding work see eslint + tsc integrated automatically into Construction; Inception/Operation markdown writes get `required-sections` + `upstream-coverage` advisory checks. Workflow continues advisory — no gate veto, no blocking; the ralph driver upgrades this to blocking semantics for Construction-phase sensors in a later release.

G1.5 lock-in: the two unscoped framework manifests gain `matches: "**/aidlc-docs/**"` (the leading `**/` consumes any absolute-path prefix Claude Code passes via `tool_input.file_path`; the trailing `/**` matches every artifact under `aidlc-docs/` at any depth, including flat `aidlc-docs/foo.md` paths). Manifest declares its own scope; no hook-side default. The compile snapshots `matches` from each manifest into every importing stage's `sensors_applicable[].matches`, so the hook reads cached glob strings without re-opening manifests at fire time. The `**/aidlc-docs/**` form (vs the draft `**/aidlc-docs/**/*.md`) is load-bearing: the dispatcher uses a home-grown `globToRegex` that translates `**` → `.*` and rejects flat-aidlc-docs paths under the `*.md`-suffixed form, even though `Bun.Glob` (the hook's matcher) accepts both. Two glob engines, one common form.

**Three forward-notes:**

* **`runtime-graph.json` `sensor_firings[]` population deferred.** This release ships the surface that emits `SENSOR_*` audit rows via the dispatcher; `aidlc-runtime.ts:319` continues to hardcode `sensor_firings: []` on every compiled `RuntimeStage`. A later gate ritual is the first consumer that walks `audit.md` since each stage's `started_at` to populate the array.
* **First-fire banner deferred.** A one-line stderr banner on first invocation against a workspace pointing users at `docs/guide/<NN>-learning-loop.md` is envisioned. The doc ships later; banner with no link is dead weight, so it lands together.
* **`sensor-fire.last` mtime semantics for the doctor.** The hook touches `aidlc-docs/.aidlc-hooks-health/sensor-fire.last` after passing the input + recursion + audit-existence + state + test-run-mode guards but BEFORE the active-stage and graph-read guards. This means "fresh heartbeat + zero `SENSOR_FIRED` rows" can mean either (a) healthy hook firing on a stage with empty `sensors_applicable` like `workspace-scaffold`, or (b) hook crash mid-dispatch. The doctor must distinguish by reading `Current Stage` from state, looking up the stage's `sensors_applicable` length, and only flagging when (`length > 0` AND `gap > 24h` AND intervening Write/Edit audit rows exist). The runtime-compile equivalence "post-heartbeat ≡ reached dispatch" does NOT carry to this hook because Steps 9-10 add additional post-heartbeat early-exits.

## [0.4.9] - 2026-05-28

Closes the per-Bolt fork/merge triad with its third leg. v0.4.0 shipped state-fork + audit-fork; this release adds runtime-graph fragment-fork + fragment-merge so parallel Construction Bolts each get a coherent `runtime-graph.json` entry post-merge. The orchestration sits in `aidlc-bolt.ts` `start --worktree` (after audit-fork, before the success-JSON) and `complete --merge` (after audit-merge, before the success-JSON), mirroring the existing fork/merge dance. The load-bearing piece is a `compile()` extension that populates `RuntimeStage.instances[]` for any Construction-phase stage whose `[started_at, completed_at OR now)` window contains ≥ 2 distinct `Bolt slug` values from `STATE_FORKED` rows; single-Bolt stages stay single-instance per the schema's optional `instances?` reservation. Audit count stays at **61** — no new event types; the fragment lifecycle rides on the existing BOLT_STARTED + STATE_FORKED + AUDIT_FORKED (fork) and BOLT_COMPLETED + STATE_MERGED + AUDIT_MERGED (merge) boundaries.

The fragment file lives at `<worktree>/aidlc-docs/runtime-graph.json` (gitignored, mirrors main). It's substrate-only in v0.5.0 — no v0.5.0 reader; v0.6.0's `--resume` is the consumer. fragment-fork's source-absent fallback (brownfield projects with no main runtime-graph.json yet) writes an empty graph anchored to the worktree's state cursor and emits `source_present: false` on stdout. fragment-merge is idempotent: re-runs after a successful merge or against a Bolt whose fragment-fork step failed exit cleanly with `status: "fragment-absent"`. Defense-in-depth removal pairs explicit fragment-merge during `complete --merge` with the implicit `git worktree remove` invoked by `aidlc-worktree merge` / `discard` — same pattern state-merge uses on the state side.

**Three forward-notes:**

* **`instances[].sensor_firings[]` per-Bolt attribution deferred.** This release introduces the per-Bolt nesting via `BoltInstance[]`, which means a later compile patch must populate BOTH the parent stage's `sensor_firings[]` AND each `BoltInstance.sensor_firings[]`. The parent rule is straightforward (per-stage filter by Timestamp window); the per-instance rule needs an attribution mechanism, likely Output-path under the Bolt's worktree path. This release leaves both empty arrays in lockstep so the next consumer sees a uniform substrate.
* **`instances[].memory_entries` + `memory_breakdown` deferred to per-stage memory.md lifecycle.** Per-Bolt memory.md doesn't exist yet; the per-stage memory.md lifecycle ships that shape in a later release. Every BoltInstance currently emits both fields as `null` (matches the v0.4.0 backfill rule — null = no per-Bolt memory.md history).
* **Defense-in-depth fragment removal is documented but not relied on.** The worktree fragment is removed by `aidlc-runtime fragment-merge` during `complete --merge` AND transitively by `git worktree remove` during `aidlc-worktree merge` / `discard`. The pair mirrors how state-merge + `git worktree remove` already pair on the state side. If fragment-merge fails after audit-merge succeeds, the unusual `BOLT_COMPLETED → STATE_MERGED → AUDIT_MERGED → BOLT_FAILED (Reason: fragment-merge-failed)` audit signature is the recovery surface; subsequent compile against main produces a coherent runtime-graph (the BOLT_FAILED at this position scores the instance `"approved"` because STATE_MERGED is already on record).

# aidlc-workflows 0.5.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.5.0] - 2026-05-31

**The framework now learns from you, checks the work automatically, and is reshapeable without writing code.** Two things change for anyone running `/aidlc`: every approval gate now offers to capture what you corrected so the same correction is never needed twice, and deterministic checks (linter, type-check, required document sections, upstream coverage) fire automatically as agents write — an advisory second opinion you never have to ask for. The larger change is for harness engineers: stages, agents, scopes, rules, and sensors are all editable declarative files now, so you can reshape how AI-DLC behaves for your team by editing Markdown and JSON — no TypeScript. A new Harness Engineer Guide documents exactly that. Under the hood, this is the control-plane / data-plane cut: one compile at workflow start resolves rules and sensors per stage, and a runtime graph mirrors each run. This release also carries a **BREAKING** rename — every framework file now has an `aidlc-` prefix and the rules directory is flat (the `.claude/practices/` folder is gone). This entry consolidates the `0.4.1` → `0.4.13` patches; those headings stay below for historical reference.

**Upgrade.** Re-copy `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/` over your project's `.claude/`. Framework files now carry an `aidlc-` prefix and the rules directory is flat — re-target any customisations from `.claude/practices/` or `.claude/rules/aidlc/guardrails/` to `.claude/rules/aidlc-<scope>.md`, and rename hand-authored hooks that pin the old unprefixed hook filenames. The state template is unchanged from v0.4.0 (v7), so existing workspaces stay schema-compatible. A workspace mid-workflow with overlay customisations you can't easily re-target archives and re-inits per the pre-1.0 no-migration policy:

    mv aidlc-docs aidlc-docs-v04-archive && /aidlc --init --force --scope <scope>

**For everyone running `/aidlc`**

* **Gates now capture what you teach them.** Between a stage finishing and you approving it, the framework surfaces what the agent noticed during the stage — interpretations it had to make, places it deviated, tradeoffs it weighed — and asks "anything to add for next time?" You tick what is worth keeping and pick one of four headings; the framework saves it as a standing rule so the correction carries into the next workflow. Most stages surface nothing, which is healthy — the prompt only has substance when something genuinely came up. See [Rules and the Learning Loop](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/08-rules-and-the-learning-loop.md).
* **Automatic checks on every file write.** Four deterministic sensors — a linter, a type-checker, a required-sections check, and an upstream-coverage check — now run by themselves whenever an agent writes a stage's output. They are advisory: a finding leaves a note in the audit log pointing at exactly what is missing, but it never blocks your gate. The first time one fires in a workspace, a one-line banner points you at the guide.
* **`/aidlc --doctor --rule-drift`** flags where your team or project rules have drifted from the framework defaults — it quotes the conflicting default inline so you can review it. Advisory; it never fails the health check.
* **Architecture choices now get a written trade-off.** When a design decision has more than one viable approach, the design stage lays out Option A / Option B with reversibility and a recommendation tied to your non-functional requirements, then records the rejected alternatives in the ADR.
* **Richer post-compaction recovery.** A fresh session after a compaction can reconstruct more of where a workflow was, by reading the artifact tree, each stage's observation diary, the audit log, the state docs, and the new runtime graph.

**For harness engineers — reshape AI-DLC without code**

* **A new [Harness Engineer Guide](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/HEAD/docs/harness-engineering/00-overview.md)** (`docs/harness-engineering/`, 8 chapters) is the headline. It walks through every change you can make by editing declarative files rather than TypeScript: the anatomy of a stage, adding a stage, adding an agent, defining a scope, authoring rules, authoring sensors, and giving agents team knowledge.
* **Rules are flat, layered Markdown you can read and edit.** `.claude/rules/aidlc-{org,team,project}.md` plus a file per phase. Scope comes from the filename — no `scope:` field. Resolution is **strict-additive**: every applicable rule from org → team → project → phase reaches the agent, nothing is silently overridden. The old `enforcement:` / `overrides:` keywords are gone; conflicts are caught when a rule is written, not hidden at runtime.
* **Sensors are authorable, and stages choose which ones fire.** A sensor is a small Markdown manifest under `.claude/sensors/` describing a check and how to run it. It says nothing about which stages use it — a stage imports the sensors it wants through a `sensors:` list in its frontmatter. Author a manifest, add its id to a stage, and the check rides along on that stage's file writes. The four shipped sensors are the worked examples.
* **The learning loop can wire a sensor in for you.** When a captured learning is "this stage should always run check X," the framework scaffolds the sensor manifest and adds it to that stage's `sensors:` import in one step.
* **Stages, agents, and scopes stay declarative.** A stage is a Markdown file with a frontmatter contract (what it consumes, produces, and which agent leads it); an agent is a persona file; a scope is an entry in `scope-mapping.json` deciding which of the 32 stages run for a kind of work. Editing any of them is a data change, documented end-to-end in the new guide.

**For developers — under the hood**

* **Control plane.** `aidlc-graph.ts compile` walks `.claude/rules/` and `.claude/sensors/` at workflow start, resolves the five-layer chain per stage, and bakes `rules_in_context` + `sensors_applicable` into every node of `stage-graph.json`. Runs under `withAuditLock` with atomic temp-rename writes. The `enforcement:` / `overrides:` keywords are removed; admission-time conflict checks (practices-discovery, the learning gate) replace runtime override resolution.
* **Data plane.** A new tool, `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-runtime.ts` (`compile` / `read`, plus `fragment-fork` / `fragment-merge` for parallel Construction Bolts), materialises a per-workflow `runtime-graph.json` by walking `audit.md` + per-stage `memory.md`. A PostToolUse hook recompiles it deterministically after every gate/transition write.
* **Sensor dispatch.** `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-sensor.ts` (`list` / `describe` / `fire`) routes to the four per-sensor scripts; the `aidlc-sensor-fire.ts` PostToolUse hook reads the active stage's `sensors_applicable` and fires the matching sensors on Write/Edit.
* **The learning gate is a tool.** `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-learnings.ts` (`surface` / `persist`) reads a stage's `memory.md`, emits candidates for the orchestrator's AskUserQuestion, and writes confirmed learnings to `.claude/rules/aidlc-{project,team}-learnings.md` — plus the two-write sensor bind — inside one `withAuditLock`.
* **Two new framework hooks (7 → 9):** `aidlc-sensor-fire.ts` and `aidlc-runtime-compile.ts`.
* **Test coverage for the learning-gate call seam.** `t86` now also pins the `SKILL.md` Stage-Advancement wiring that makes the orchestrator actually invoke `aidlc-learnings.ts surface` + `persist` at a gate (TEST_RUN_MODE-guarded), plus the Test-Run-block skip declaration — closing the gap where the tool (`t97`/`t99`) and the §13 prose (`t86`) could both pass while the orchestrator never called the gate.
* **Audit taxonomy 55 → 61 events.** Five sensor slots pre-registered, `MEMORY_EMPTY` for silent-diary detection, four `SENSOR_*` emitters wired, `RULE_LEARNED` + `SENSOR_PROPOSED` for the learning gate, and `GUARDRAIL_LOADED` for the doctor coverage row. The dead guardrail-*learning* subsystem (`GUARDRAIL_TRIGGERED` / `GUARDRAIL_LEARNED`, `aidlc-guardrail.ts`) was retired, netting 61. If you grepped audit logs for the two retired events, those rows are no longer emitted.
* **BREAKING — `aidlc-` filename prefix + flat rules layout + practices folder removed.** Every framework-shipped file under `.claude/` (tools, hooks, agents, knowledge directories) carries an `aidlc-` prefix. `.claude/rules/aidlc/{guardrails,phases}/` flattens to `.claude/rules/aidlc-{org,team,project,phase-<phase>}.md`; `.claude/practices/` is removed (team config now lives in `.claude/rules/aidlc-team.md`). `aidlc-knowledge/` becomes `knowledge/` with `aidlc-<role>-agent/` and `aidlc-shared/` subdirectories.
* **Documentation + install.** Docs are split three ways by reader — User Guide, Harness Engineer Guide, Developer Reference — all linked from the README. Install switched to Claude Code's native installer, Getting Started gains a full AWS Bedrock Setup section, and the shipped `.claude/settings.json` now sets `AWS_REGION`.
* `aidlc-claude-code/.claude/tools/aidlc-version.ts` — bumped 0.4.13 → 0.5.0.

# aidlc-workflows 0.5.14

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.5.14] - 2026-06-04

Adds the framework's first flow-altering hook: a `Stop` hook (`aidlc-stop.ts`, wired into the `aidlc` skill frontmatter) that enforces the interactive forwarding loop. When the conductor tries to end its turn, the hook runs the orchestration engine (`aidlc-orchestrate next`); if the workflow is complete (`done`) it lets the turn end, and if a step is still pending it blocks the stop and re-feeds the next move so the loop runs to completion regardless of whether the LLM remembered to consult the engine. The injected message is phrased only as the work still owed — never an override-shaped instruction — so a buggy or compromised engine can only ever continue sanctioned work, never hijack the session. Recursion is bounded two ways so a stuck loop can never trap a session: a no-progress block counter under an 8-block ceiling (`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`, default 8) and Claude Code's own `stop_hook_active` signal; once the ceiling is reached the hook releases the turn. User interrupt (Esc) is never affected — Stop hooks do not fire on interrupt. The hook is a no-op outside an AIDLC workflow and fails open on any unexpected error, so a non-AIDLC session is never blocked. No upgrade action required.

* The shipped `aidlc` skill now registers a `Stop` hook. On the interactive path the forwarding loop is harness-enforced: a turn that ends with a pending workflow step is blocked and the next step is injected back, until the engine reports the workflow is `done`. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` to tune the recursion ceiling (default 8); when the no-progress block streak reaches it, the hook lets the turn end. The hook does nothing outside an AIDLC workflow and never affects a manual interrupt.
* The framework now ships 10 hooks (was 9).

# aidlc-workflows 0.5.15

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.5.15] - 2026-06-04

Restores `--test-run` persistence at both workflow birth AND resume, which the orchestration-engine cutover (0.5.12) silently dropped on both legs. When that release moved orchestration from `SKILL.md` prose into the engine, two re-stamp paths were lost. (1) Birth: the engine's `--init` directive builder threaded `--scope`/`--depth`/`--force` but not `--test-run` — so `/aidlc <scope> --test-run` scaffolded state WITHOUT the `Test Run Mode: true` field that `init` writes only when it receives the flag. (2) Resume: the old prose ran `aidlc-utility.ts enable-test-run` whenever `--test-run` re-entered an already-scaffolded workflow, re-stamping the field; the cutover deleted that instruction with no replacement, so a `--test-run` resume over a stamp-less workflow never re-stamped. That field is what the jump tool reads on resume to detect test-run mode (it reads the field, not the CLI flag), so either drop meant a `--test-run` run could lose its automation marking and start prompting at gates. The engine now restores both: it threads `--test-run` into the scaffold command at birth, and on resume it emits a run-then-continue `print` naming `enable-test-run` when `--test-run` re-enters a workflow whose state lacks the field — the same engine-names-the-move / conductor-runs-the-tool shape it already uses for scope-change and jumps, so `next` stays read-only. This makes good on 0.5.12's "behaviour is unchanged" promise. No action is needed for existing workflows. No upgrade action required.

* `/aidlc <scope> --test-run` (and `/aidlc --init --test-run`) once again records `Test Run Mode: true` in `aidlc-docs/aidlc-state.md` at workflow birth, so test-run mode survives across resume in a fresh session.
* `/aidlc <scope> --test-run` re-entering an EXISTING workflow whose state file lacks the `Test Run Mode` field (e.g. a workflow first started without `--test-run`, then resumed with it) now re-persists the field instead of silently running without it — restoring the resume-time `enable-test-run` re-stamp the prose orchestrator ran before the cutover. Between 0.5.12 and this release the flag was dropped on both the birth and resume legs, so an automated/CI run could lose its test-run marking and start prompting at gates.
