# aidlc-workflows 0.5.20

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.5.20] - 2026-06-06

Ships the swarm's deterministic convergence **referee**, `aidlc-swarm.ts`. The swarm fires only under human-granted Construction autonomy inside a live `/aidlc` session, so the conductor (that session) owns the fan-out and the retry loop; the tool owns only what must be deterministic — the convergence verdict, the anti-tamper guard, the serialised merge-back, and the typed failure envelope. It is stateless (no iteration counter) and re-exposed as three subcommands. `prepare` forks an isolated git worktree per unit (composing `aidlc-worktree create` + `aidlc-bolt start --worktree`) and records batch start. `check <unit>` returns a stateless verdict from the project's own check command (exit 0 = green — a worker's self-claim is never trusted) plus an anti-tamper compare of a protected file against its forked-git baseline. `finalize --claimed` re-verifies every unit the conductor claims converged before any merge, serialised-merges only the genuine passes (the existing HOLD-MERGE lock), and returns the typed envelope (`unsatisfiable`, `budget-exhausted`, `cap-exhausted`, `error`). Because `finalize` re-verifies, a red unit cannot merge even if the conductor lies or misremembers — the lying-conductor guard. Nothing invokes the referee automatically yet; it is wired to the conductor in v0.5.21. No upgrade action.

* New tool surface `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-swarm.ts prepare|check|finalize`. `prepare --batch <n> --units <a,b,c> [--base <branch>] [--degraded-from <subagent|ultracode>]` forks the worktrees; `check <unit> --check-cmd <cmd> [--test-file <path>]` prints `{converged, tampered, reason}` and exits 0 iff genuinely converged (emits no audit); `finalize --batch <n> --units <a,b,c> --claimed <a,b> --check-cmd <cmd> [--test-file <path>] [--reasons <unit>=<reason>,…]` prints the JSON envelope (`{units, converged, failed, merge_failures}`) and exits 0 when every claimed unit re-verified and merged, 2 when any unit failed or a merge failed (the conductor takes the baton). `--reasons` lets the conductor attribute a typed reason (`unsatisfiable` / `budget-exhausted` / `cap-exhausted`) to a *declined* unit it did not claim — recorded faithfully on `SWARM_UNIT_FAILED`, defaulting to `cap-exhausted`, and never able to override a claimed-but-red unit's `error` verdict. The retired headless `run` verb, the `claude -p` worker, the triple cap, and the `AIDLC_SWARM_CLAUDE_BIN` test seam are all gone — the runaway backstop is now the harness 8-block Stop-hook ceiling.
* A new audit event `SWARM_DEGRADED` records a loud downgrade — `AIDLC_USE_SWARM=1` was requested but the Workflow tool was unavailable, so the conductor ran the subagent floor (the referee makes the substrate difference invisible to convergence). The two previously-reserved per-Unit events now emit from `finalize`: `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED` (re-verified green and untampered) and `SWARM_UNIT_FAILED` (not claimed, claimed-but-red, or tampered, with the typed reason). The batch-level trio stays reserved until the conductor wiring lands. The audit taxonomy grows from 66 to 67 events.

**The orchestrator is unbundled: a deterministic engine decides what happens next, the `/aidlc` session carries it out, and the framework gained a family of typeable runner commands plus an autonomous build swarm.** For everyone running `/aidlc`, invocation is unchanged — the recomposition is internal. What's new is the surface around it: one-word `/aidlc-<stage>` and `/aidlc-<scope>` runner commands; a `--single` mode that runs a stage in isolation without touching your workflow; and, under human-granted Construction autonomy, a swarm that fans out independent build units in parallel and converges them behind a deterministic referee. Under the hood, the routing logic moved out of `SKILL.md` (now a ~170-line forwarding loop) into the `aidlc-orchestrate` engine, which emits a typed directive on every turn; scope membership is now file-authored (`.claude/scopes/aidlc-<name>.md` + a `scopes:` tag on each stage) and the old `scope-mapping.json` is gone.

**Upgrade.** Re-copy the shipped `.claude/` over your project's `.claude/` (`cp -r dist/claude/.claude/ your-project/.claude/`). Because every framework hook is now registered project-wide in `settings.json` (the skill-scoped hooks moved there), re-copy the shipped `settings.json` or merge its `hooks` block so the relocated hooks are registered — `aidlc/SKILL.md` no longer carries a `hooks:` block. The state template is unchanged, so existing workspaces stay schema-compatible.

**For everyone running `/aidlc`**

* **`/aidlc` works exactly as before** — full orchestrator, scope detection, every flag. No breaking changes to how you invoke a workflow.
* **New `/aidlc-<scope>` runner commands.** `/aidlc-bugfix`, `/aidlc-feature`, `/aidlc-mvp`, `/aidlc-security-patch` drive a workflow with a fixed scope and no detection — the same workflow as `/aidlc --scope <name>`, as their own typeable command. Every other scope stays reachable via `/aidlc --scope <name>`.
* **New `/aidlc-<stage>` runner commands + `--single`.** One command per runnable stage (e.g. `/aidlc-code-generation`) runs that stage in isolation via `--single` and never advances your main workflow's stage pointer — the isolation is tool-enforced. `/aidlc-init` packages `/aidlc --init`.
* **An autonomous build swarm.** After you grant Construction autonomy, eligible independent build units fan out in parallel (across isolated worktrees) and converge behind a deterministic referee that re-verifies every unit before merge — a unit that fails, or is falsely claimed converged, returns the baton to you. Set `AIDLC_USE_SWARM=1` to drive the fan-out with an inline workflow; unset it for the parallel-subagent floor.
* **Skill-picker discoverability.** Every `/aidlc-*` runner surfaces in Claude Code's `/` picker, no manual registration.

**For harness engineers and contributors**

* **Scope is a file-authored primitive.** A scope is a `.claude/scopes/aidlc-<name>.md` file (identity) plus a `scopes:` tag on each member stage (membership), transposed at compile into `scope-grid.json`. The `scope-mapping.json` data file is removed; adding a scope is now purely additive, no code edit.
* **Runners are generated, not hand-written.** `aidlc-runner-gen.ts` emits a runner per runnable stage and per shipped scope from the compiled graph; drift guards fail CI if the on-disk set diverges. "To add a stage, write a stage file" then regenerate — the runner follows.
* **The orchestration engine + typed directive contract.** `aidlc-orchestrate.ts` (`next`/`report`) owns all between-stage routing and emits a validated typed directive; `SKILL.md` is the conductor that acts on it. New reference chapter [Engine and Skill System](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/17-skill-system.md) and User Guide chapter [Skills and Runner Commands](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/17-skills.md) document both.
* **Audit taxonomy grows to 67 events** — six `SWARM_*` events for the batch lifecycle (`SWARM_STARTED`, `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED`, `SWARM_UNIT_FAILED`, `SWARM_BATON_RETURNED`, `SWARM_COMPLETED`, `SWARM_DEGRADED`).
* `dist/claude/.claude/tools/aidlc-version.ts` — bumped 0.5.21 → 0.6.0.

# aidlc-workflows 0.7.8

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [0.7.8] - 2026-06-16

Stops the interactive `/aidlc` Stop hook from spamming the forwarding-loop nudge while you are answering a gate. When the conductor parks at an approval gate or in the Request-Changes loop, it ends its turn waiting for you — but the engine still reports the stage as in-flight, so the forwarding-loop Stop hook used to block the stop and re-inject the "you haven't finished the forwarding loop" nudge repeatedly until its 8-block cap bled out. The hook now reads the current stage's checkbox state and **allows** the stop when the stage is awaiting approval (`[?]`) or being revised (`[R]`) — the two states that exist only because the workflow is waiting on you. This is a positive-confirmation, fail-open carve-out: it only ever releases the stop more readily, never blocks more; a genuine mid-stage quit (or any other state) still falls through to the existing cap-bounded block. One core edit fixes the Claude and Kiro (and Codex) harnesses; re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` to pick it up.

* **Interactive approval gates and the Request-Changes loop no longer emit the repeated forwarding-loop nudge.** Previously up to ~8 "Stop hook" nudges could appear at a single gate while you typed your answer; now the hook allows the stop as soon as it sees the stage is awaiting approval or being revised.
* **Known follow-up — a mid-stage clarifying question still relies on the cap.** A question asked *before* the gate leaves the stage `[-]` in-progress, which is indistinguishable from a lazy mid-stage quit by checkbox state alone, so it is deliberately NOT carved out (a blanket `[-]` carve-out would gut the hook). The safe fix needs an engine-side "question pending" signal and is tracked as a follow-up. Immediate mitigation for either case: set `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP=1` (or `=2`) in `.claude/settings.local.json` `env` (or export it) to collapse the spam to a single nudge.
* No CLI surface change; no new commands or flags. The recursion bounds (`stop_hook_active`, the no-progress counter, and `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`) are unchanged.

# aidlc-workflows 2.1.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.1.0] - 2026-06-24

Moves AI-DLC from a single flat `aidlc-docs/` record to a per-intent **workspace** layout: spaces, multiple coexisting intents, multi-repo, space-level knowledge and code-KB, and a method (memory) that follows the active space. A project root now holds `aidlc/spaces/<space>/intents/<slug>-<id8>/`, so many intents (and non-default spaces) live side by side without colliding; read-only/navigation `/aidlc` commands are reliable mid-workflow. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project — it ships the workspace pre-scaffolded, so there is no more `/aidlc --init` (the engine auto-births the first intent on your first `/aidlc`). A project still on the old flat `aidlc-docs/` layout is migrated automatically and crash-safely on first run (copy → atomic rename into the per-intent record; the tracked flat tree is git-rm'd post-move; idempotent on a `.migrated` marker). The audit trail is now **committed as per-clone shards** (`intents/<id>/audit/<host>-<clone>.md`) rather than a single `audit.md`, so concurrent clones never merge-conflict the trail; readers glob and merge by timestamp. A confirmed learning now lands as a **practice** in the relocated `aidlc/spaces/<space>/memory/` (the `*-learnings.md` files are gone), and team **domain knowledge** is **space-level** at `aidlc/spaces/<space>/knowledge/` (a free-form, empty-at-bootstrap sibling of memory/codekb/intents, shared across every intent in the space; a migrating project's flat `aidlc-docs/knowledge/` is relocated there automatically — the engine's per-agent methodology knowledge stays shipped under `<harness>/knowledge/`). This release rebases onto and consolidates the v2 line (reviewer mechanism + Kiro IDE harness, 2.0.0–2.0.2), so it ships the 13-agent roster and both Kiro distributions alongside the workspace refactor. A new user-guide chapter, [Spaces and Intents](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/03-spaces-and-intents.md), documents the model.

**Workspace layout**

* `/aidlc --init` is **retired** — the shipped shell scaffolds the workspace and the first intent auto-births; `--force`/state-wipe is gone. Re-copy `dist/<harness>/`.
* `--repo`/`--repos` make an intent multi-repo: the repo set is captured at birth and Construction worktrees fork against the right sibling repo.
* The record tree, audit shards, `intents.json`, memory, codekb, and knowledge are committed; the per-user cursors (`active-space`, `active-intent`) and machine-local runtime are gitignored.
* **CI/scripts (breaking):** the flat `aidlc-docs/` path no longer resolves for new projects — resolve state/audit/artifacts under `aidlc/spaces/<space>/intents/<slug>-<id8>/` (the migration keys on `aidlc-docs/aidlc-state.md` as its sole detection trigger).
* Engine-only installs self-heal: if the `aidlc/` workspace shell wasn't copied alongside the engine dir, the first `/aidlc` seeds `aidlc/spaces/default/memory/` from a copy bundled in the engine (idempotent — a normal install that copied `aidlc/` is left untouched).

**Navigation verbs**

* New intent + space verbs: `/aidlc intent` (list/switch), `/aidlc space` (list/switch), `/aidlc space-create <name>`, `/aidlc intent-birth`; a `--json` query layer on the list handlers. They route through the conductor and are recognised only as the LEADING token, so a freeform request that merely contains "space" or "intent" mid-sentence (e.g. `/aidlc add a settings space`) is still treated as new-work input.
* While an intent is active, describing a genuinely new, unrelated piece of work prompts the orchestrator to **offer a second intent alongside** (you confirm Y/n before anything is born); switch between them any time with `/aidlc intent <name>`.

**Active-space following**

* `/aidlc space <name>` re-points the active harness's rule include (Claude `@`-stub, Kiro `agents/*.json` resources glob, Codex `AIDLC_RULES_DIR`) to the switched space — the next turn loads that space's method into ambient context. The includes stay committed and are re-pointed in place; at `default` the re-point is a byte-identical no-op, so a single-team committed tree never churns.
* The method resolver and the learnings/practices writers follow the active space: a learning promoted under `active-space=<name>` lands in `aidlc/spaces/<name>/memory/`; a cursorless resolve still yields `default`.
* `/aidlc space-create <name>` seeds the full space shape — `codekb/` and `knowledge/` siblings (with `.gitkeep` floors) alongside `memory/` and `intents/`, matching `default`.
* The `required-sections` sensor and the stage-protocol template clause resolve templates as team → framework-default → generic floor (override-before-default). No framework-default templates ship at GA, so resolution is unchanged until one is authored.

**Per-repo code knowledge base**

* New read-only `/aidlc codekb-path [--repo <name>] [--json]` verb prints the deterministic per-repo codekb directory without mutating state.
* Reverse-engineering's 9 artifacts now land at the space-level per-repo path `aidlc/spaces/<space>/codekb/<repo>/` — a durable store shared across every intent in the space — rather than at the agent's discretion under the per-intent record dir.

**Kiro read-only/navigation determinism**

* On Kiro, `/aidlc --status` / `--doctor` / `--help` / `--version` and `/aidlc space` / `space-create <name>` / `intent <name>` now run reliably while a workflow is active — they print/switch as documented instead of occasionally advancing the active intent. A `userPromptSubmit` hook runs these deterministic commands directly; re-copy your `dist/kiro/` shell to pick up the new hooks (`agents/aidlc.json` → `hooks.userPromptSubmit`, plus a `hooks.preToolUse` backstop).
* The dispatch is enforced by a turn-scoped guard: the engine emits a terminal stop (and a Kiro `preToolUse` backstop blocks) when a bare `next` would otherwise roll a workflow forward in the same turn a read-only/navigation command was already handled. On every harness the `next --status` / `--doctor` / `--help` / `--version` print directive now names the exact `aidlc-utility.ts` subcommand and instructs the conductor to stop.
* Mutating commands are unaffected: `--scope` / `--test-strategy` changes and intent birth still run and then resume the workflow.

# aidlc-workflows 2.1.3

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.1.3] - 2026-06-28

Closes the rubber-stamp trap that let an agent on a long (enterprise-scope) workflow mark every remaining stage complete with no real output, and stops the Stop hook from nagging a human who just wants to chat mid-workflow. Four interlocking fixes land together (they all touch `aidlc-state.ts` / the Stop hook, so shipping separately would force hard conflicts): a first-class **park** command gives the conductor a clean multi-session exit, a deterministic **artifact guard** refuses to complete a stage with no evidence of work on disk, an **autonomy guard** keeps an unattended swarm/Bolt run from self-parking, and a **conversational carve-out** lets a chat turn end without being nudged back into the loop. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project. CI/scripts breaking change: every `aidlc-state.ts` subcommand that completes a stage (`approve`, `advance`, `finalize`, `complete-workflow`) now refuses to mark it `[x]` when the stage's declared `produces[]` artifacts are absent; pass `--test-run` or set `AIDLC_SKIP_ARTIFACT_GUARD=1` for automated dry runs.

* **Park (#365, #367):** `bun .claude/tools/aidlc-orchestrate.ts park` parks the workflow at the current inter-stage boundary and emits a new `parked` directive; the Stop hook treats `parked` as a terminal allow, so a long workflow can pause and resume in a later session with `/aidlc --resume` instead of rubber-stamping stages to reach `done`. No stage is advanced and nothing is marked complete.
* **Artifact guard (#366):** `approve`, `advance`, `finalize`, and `complete-workflow` now verify on-disk evidence before marking a stage `[x]`: a declared `produces[]` artifact must exist under the intent's record dir, and a `workspace_requires` stage (today only `code-generation`) must additionally show real source work outside the `aidlc/` workspace tree (git-aware when the workspace is a git repo, else a filesystem-existence check). Bypass with `--test-run` or `AIDLC_SKIP_ARTIFACT_GUARD=1`.
* **Autonomy guard (#365):** an autonomous Construction run (`Construction Autonomy Mode: autonomous`) can never self-park: both `aidlc-state.ts park` and the Stop hook's `parked` allow decline under autonomous mode, so an unattended run keeps moving.
* **Conversational carve-out (#365):** the Stop hook no longer nags a human who is just chatting mid-workflow. When the harness delivers a transcript (Claude and Codex pass `transcript_path`), the hook reads it and, if the most recent human prompt was answered with no workflow-engine call (`aidlc-orchestrate` / `aidlc-state`), it allows the turn to end with zero nudges. As a portable backstop on every harness (including Kiro, which delivers no transcript), the no-progress block cap now defaults to **2 in an interactive run** (down from 8 - issue #365's own recommended workaround) so a chatting or pausing human is released after one nudge; an **autonomous** Construction run keeps the long cap of 8 and the carve-out is disabled there (the unattended loop must keep moving). `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` still overrides both.
* New audit events `WORKFLOW_PARKED` / `WORKFLOW_UNPARKED` and state subcommands `park` / `unpark`; the audit taxonomy grows from 67 to 69 events.

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.1.6] - 2026-07-03

Gates the approval and interview checkpoints on deterministic proof that a real human acted (issue #451). Deep into a long session, an agent under an autonomous IDE mode (observed on the Kiro IDE harness with autopilot) could fabricate the user's own approval ("Approve") or interview answer inside one un-ended turn and advance the workflow, because the gate recorded the conductor-supplied `--user-input` verbatim after only the artifact-existence check (issue #366) with no check that a human actually responded. Now a real human prompt records a `HUMAN_TURN` event in the audit ledger, and the approve/answer gate refuses unless a `HUMAN_TURN` was recorded since the last gate resolution (`GATE_APPROVED` / `GATE_REJECTED` / `QUESTION_ANSWERED`) in ledger order. There is no marker file, no turn counter, and no consumed flag: the ledger itself is the record. On the Kiro CLI and Kiro IDE harnesses a `preToolUse` hook hard-blocks tool calls while a gate is open and no human has acted since, as the enforcement floor. The gate is scoped off under autonomous Construction (swarm / Bolt) so unattended runs do not deadlock, and fail-opens on an empty ledger, so existing flows are unaffected until a `HUMAN_TURN` has been recorded. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project; no action is needed for normal interactive use. For synthetic CI that drives `approve`/`answer` against bare fixtures with no human turn, set `AIDLC_SKIP_HUMAN_PRESENCE_GUARD=1` (mirrors the existing `AIDLC_SKIP_ARTIFACT_GUARD`).

* `aidlc-state.ts approve` and `aidlc-log.ts answer` now refuse to commit unless a real human acted at the checkpoint: the gate scans the audit ledger and requires a `HUMAN_TURN` event recorded since the last gate resolution (`GATE_APPROVED` / `GATE_REJECTED` / `QUESTION_ANSWERED`), so a fabricated cascade in one un-ended turn cannot rubber-stamp multiple gates. Refusals exit non-zero and leave state untouched.
* Per-harness mint seam: the prompt-submit hook records a `HUMAN_TURN` audit event on Claude (new `UserPromptSubmit` hook `aidlc-mint-presence.ts`, also fired on every answered `AskUserQuestion` widget so clicking Approve or answering an interview question counts as human presence), Kiro IDE (new `promptSubmit` hook), Codex (`user_prompt_submit`), and Kiro CLI. The mint is a no-op in a project with no active workflow state, so carrying the harness shell without running AI-DLC never creates audit files.
* The Kiro CLI and Kiro IDE harnesses also ship a `preToolUse` hook that hard-blocks tool calls (exit code 2) while a stage actually awaits approval (`[?]`) and no human has acted since the last gate resolution; after a legitimate approval the floor stands down so the same-turn advance into the next stage proceeds normally.
* Autonomous Construction (`Construction Autonomy Mode: autonomous`, i.e. swarm / Bolt) is exempt: the gate does not require a human there, so unattended runs never deadlock. An empty ledger fails open (the gate is enforced only once a `HUMAN_TURN` has been recorded). The presence check orders ledger events chronologically across audit shards, so a second clone's committed shard (a re-clone or another machine) never masks a fresh human turn.
* New bypass `AIDLC_SKIP_HUMAN_PRESENCE_GUARD=1` for synthetic CI runs that drive transitions against bare fixtures with no human turn (mirrors `AIDLC_SKIP_ARTIFACT_GUARD=1`); it disables the approve/answer gate and the Kiro `preToolUse` floors alike.

## [2.1.7] - 2026-07-03

Closes the dangling-consume gaps behind the incremental scopes (issue #461). The lean scopes deliberately skip upstream producer stages, but three downstream consumers of the stage `consumes:` contracts did not honor that design: the run-stage directive pointed the executing agent at input files that can never exist (leaving the fallback to per-run improvisation), the upstream-coverage sensor demanded the output prose reference artifacts that were never produced (a guaranteed recurring `SENSOR_FAILED` in six scopes), and nothing distinguished a deliberate scope shortcut from an accidental new dangling edge. Also widens `security-patch` with `requirements-analysis` — the one dangling edge with no in-scope substitute — so a CVE response records an auditable statement of the vulnerability and its remediation criteria. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* `security-patch` now includes `requirements-analysis` (10 of 32 stages, was 9). The `requirements` artifact that `nfr-requirements` and `code-generation` hard-require now has an in-scope producer; the scope stays Minimal depth so the requirements pass scales with the patch.
* The run-stage directive splits declared inputs by on-disk presence: `consumes` lists only inputs that exist; a new optional `consumes_absent` field lists the missing REQUIRED ones, each annotated `expected: true` (producer skipped by the active scope — absence is by design) or `expected: false` (producer on the path but the file is missing). Absent optional (`required: false`) inputs are dropped silently — an optional input that does not exist is not a gap. The conductor is instructed to proceed with the stage's documented fallback on expected-absent inputs and to surface unexpected gaps via the recovery protocol, instead of failing a read and improvising.
* The upstream-coverage sensor now checks only consumed artifacts that exist on disk, eliminating the false `SENSOR_FAILED` audit rows the lean scopes produced on every run of a stage whose upstream producer is skipped.
* Stage bodies that read inputs unconditionally (functional-design, nfr-requirements, nfr-design, infrastructure-design, ci-pipeline, deployment-pipeline, deployment-execution, refined-mockups, code-generation) now read each input "(if exists)" with an explicit fallback (requirements, the reverse-engineered code knowledge base, or the workspace's existing configuration), and the recovery protocol gains the producer-is-SKIP branch (re-running the producer is not an option when the scope excludes it).
* The exact per-scope advisory edge set (the deliberate producer-skipped shortcuts) is pinned in the test suite, so a new dangling required consume fails CI as a scope-authoring error instead of hiding among the accepted advisories.

Tag/source validation, deterministic packaging, static checks, native smoke coverage, cross-platform builds, lifecycle installation tests, checksums, provenance attestation, and release-candidate verification remain required.

Approval gates and human-turn checks are unchanged.

The <Stage> review did not finish.`) unless team memory locks Guard Policy strict. AI-DLC's own workflow commands run without a permission prompt or approval card on Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Kiro CLI, and Kiro IDE, while commands that change the machine's AI-DLC install ask first. On Kiro IDE, the first run walks through trusting the folder, reloading the window, and choosing the aidlc agent, a bare `/aidlc` that Kiro's menu turns into a specialist still starts AI-DLC, AI-DLC's own commands run with no approval card, and hook cards drop to one before a tool call and one after a shell command, none for a read.

Replies and refusals name `$aidlc` instead of `/aidlc`, a question box that runs out never answers for the person, and in a project shared with another tool Codex uses its own install. On opencode, setup and refreshes add only AI-DLC's entries to the team's `opencode.json`, the end-of-turn nudge and the `/aidlc` command text no longer show in the chat as the person's words, a rejected command ends the turn, and a pasted request with quotes or line breaks starts the work on every shell.
* On GitHub Copilot, AI-DLC's own commands run without an Allow click in VS Code, every step fits VS Code's 20,000-character terminal result, a Windows project carries on across VS Code's two drive-letter spellings, the chat moves on after an approval, and stage runners start only when the person types them. Cursor never throws away the person's prompt, says once which work a chat is on, says when a project is outside a git repository, and keeps background agents out of the foreground workflow. On Claude Code, the generated stage and scope runners start only when typed, and a new chat now gets the state of the work and the offer to rejoin it at session start.

# aidlc-workflows 2.2.0

## [2.2.0] - 2026-07-04

Adaptive Workflows (roadmap Goal 3): a composer agent under `/aidlc` that fits the ceremony to the task. Describe the work and the engine routes by keyword inference - a clear match gets a one-line confirm naming the matched scope, rich or unmatched prose gets a compose offer instead of the old silent feature default. The composer reads the task and the workspace scan, proposes the EXECUTE/SKIP stage grid with a per-SKIP rationale, and after your approval authors it as a scope and starts the workflow in the same turn. Point it at a scan report (`/aidlc compose --report sonar.json`) to triage findings into a compact fix-and-ship run, or run `/aidlc compose` mid-workflow to re-shape the pending stages in place. Composed scopes ship with `keywords: []` so a one-off plan never rewires future keyword routing; making a scope inferable is an explicit gate choice. (The roadmap's 2.2.0/2.3.0 assignments swap: adaptive workflows ships now as 2.2.0; reviewer-as-verifier moves to 2.3.0 and carries the Full GA declaration - this cut does NOT declare GA.) **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* NEW `/aidlc compose "<task>"` (and the `/aidlc-compose` shortcut skill): force the composer even when a stock scope matches. `--new-scope` forces synthesizing a custom scope; `--report <path>` composes from a scan report. The compose verb is deliberately NOT a workspace verb, so Kiro's off-band verb-intercept never captures it.
* Cold-start freeform routing changed: `/aidlc "<description>"` now runs keyword inference. A clear keyword hit asks a one-line confirm naming the MATCHED scope (e.g. bugfix, not feature); no hit or rich prose asks the compose offer. The old static feature-default confirm is gone.
* NEW read-only `detect` utility subcommand (`--json`): prints the workspace scan (project type, languages, frameworks, build system) plus the resolved scopes dir and scope-grid path - how the composer is told where scope data lives per harness.
* NEW `validate-grid --proposal <path> [--strict] [--project-type <t>] [--keywords <csv>]` on `aidlc-graph.ts`: validates an arbitrary EXECUTE/SKIP grid. Lenient mode mirrors `validate-scope` (off-path required producer = advisory); `--strict` (the recompose mode) hard-rejects a starved required input; `--keywords` hard-rejects any granted keyword an existing scope already claims, naming the incumbent (the composer runs this before writing gate-granted keywords). `validate-scope` behavior is unchanged.
* NEW `recompose --skip <slugs> --add <slugs>` utility subcommand: flips PENDING, ahead-of-cursor stages' plan suffixes on the live state file under the audit lock, strict-validated against NEW starvation, derived state fields rebuilt, `RECOMPOSED` audited. Rejects flips of completed/in-progress/skipped stages, behind-cursor stages, and the first EXECUTE stage of Construction (the walking-skeleton gate anchor). The rebuilt Stages-to-Skip row preserves birth's annotated entries verbatim for stages whose skip-membership did not change, so a skip+add round trip leaves the row byte-identical.
* Chat-first in-flight reshape: mid-workflow, plain chat that names skipping/dropping/adding stages of the running workflow ("can we skip market research?") is recognized by the conductor and routed through the same approve/edit/reject gate and the same `recompose` verb - no literal `compose` needed. When the request names specific stages imperatively, the conductor may present the gate directly without dispatching the composer agent (the verb's validation guards both paths identically); open-ended requests ("what can we cut?") still dispatch the composer. Never under autonomous Construction. On Kiro and Codex the literal `/aidlc compose "<request>"` verb remains the documented reliable path.
* Jump, finalize, lookup, and `--status` now honour the live plan: per-stage EXECUTE/SKIP suffix overrides (a recomposed plan) win over the static scope grid in jump target validation, the forward-skip/backward-reset loops, phase targeting, the Next Stage projections, and status counts.
* NEW `RECOMPOSED` audit event (the taxonomy is now 69 events).
* NEW `aidlc-composer-agent` (14 agents now): dispatched by the conductor for compose requests; on Kiro it ships a hand-authored agent config whose sandbox grants the two scope-registry write paths (the conductor's own sandbox still cannot write them).
* Kiro IDE: delegated subagents now get their tools. The IDE resolves a delegate's tool grants from the agent `.md` frontmatter, not from the agent-v1 JSON the Kiro CLI reads, so dispatched agents (the composer first among them) ran toolless there - "terminal tool not available". The kiro-ide packaging now injects `tools: ["read", "write", "shell"]` into the five delegation-target agent files (reviewers included - the stage protocol has them append a `## Review` section to the artifact); the other harnesses are untouched. Note the IDE grant is unscoped, wider than the CLI JSON sandbox. The composer persona also gains an explicit degraded rule: if it cannot run its deterministic steps it returns a structured failure status, never an unvalidated grid.
* Stop hook: a pending in-flight compose proposal (the conductor's `aidlc/.aidlc-compose-pending` marker) lets the turn end at the approve/edit/reject gate; autonomy-guarded and fail-open.
* The scope-grid "regenerated, never hand-edited" rule gains one carve-out: the dispatched composer appends approved composed scopes to the runtime scope registry. Note a maintainer `aidlc-graph.ts compile` still drops a composed grid entry (composed scopes have no per-stage frontmatter tags); the composer is instructed never to run compile.

# aidlc-workflows 2.2.1

## [2.2.1] - 2026-07-04

Stops help requests from accidentally creating intents. `/aidlc intent help` was parsed as "switch to an intent named help"; the failed switch died with an error inviting the agent to "describe what to build to start a new one", which a conductor mid-task read as an instruction and birthed an unwanted intent. Bare `/aidlc help` and `/aidlc -h` were worse: they fell into the freeform-description funnel and offered to birth an intent literally named "help" (or silently advanced the active stage). All help-shaped inputs now route to the help text. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* `/aidlc intent help` (or `-h`) and `/aidlc space help` (or `-h`) now print the global help instead of attempting a switch to a record named "help". Applies in the engine, the Kiro verb-intercept seam, and the `aidlc-utility.ts` handlers themselves.
* A sole bare `help` or `-h` after `/aidlc` now prints help. It no longer reaches the scope-confirmation ask on a fresh workspace or advances the active stage on a live one. `help` inside a longer description (e.g. `/aidlc "help desk app"`) is still treated as what to build.
* "help" is now a reserved record name: `intent-birth` refuses a label that slugifies to "help" and `space-create help` errors, since a record with that name could never be switched to by name. Both refusals happen before any mutation.
* The "Unknown intent" error from a failed `/aidlc intent <name>` switch no longer suggests describing new work; it points at the read-only `/aidlc intent` listing and explicitly says not to start a new workflow to recover. The "Unknown space" error likewise no longer instructs creating the missing space - creation stays a separate, deliberate move.
* The orchestrator skill's second-intent CONFIRM step named the wrong binary (`aidlc-utility.ts next ...`, which dies with a usage error listing `intent-birth` - a guard-bypass temptation); it now names `aidlc-orchestrate.ts next` on all four harnesses.
* The Codex orchestrator skill's forwarding loop now tells the conductor to drop the leading `$aidlc`/`/aidlc` invocation marker and forward the remaining text as separate arguments (observed live on Codex exec: the conductor echoed the whole slash line as one quoted token, which hid `intent help` from the router and dead-ended on a scope ask). The engine deliberately does NOT try to repair marker-prefixed input - a mangled echo lands in the scope-confirmation ask, a safe human gate.

## [2.2.10] - 2026-07-06

Workspace detection now recognizes git submodules. A workspace whose code lives in uninitialized submodules (empty dirs plus a `.gitmodules` file) previously scanned as Greenfield, so reverse-engineering was auto-skipped and every design stage ran with zero code understanding. The scanner gains a sixth brownfield signal: a parseable `.gitmodules` with at least one submodule path entry classifies the workspace Brownfield. When submodule paths are uninitialized, the scan warns and names the remedy (`git submodule update --init --recursive`) at birth, in the doctor report, and on `detect`. Languages stay as scanned (Unknown is truthful until the submodules are fetched). **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* The `WORKSPACE_SCANNED` audit event gains a `Submodules` field (`N declared, M uninitialized`) when submodules are present, and its `Details` names the `git submodule update --init --recursive` remedy when any submodule path is uninitialized. Projects without a `.gitmodules` produce a byte-identical event.
* Birth stdout prints a one-line warning when submodule paths are uninitialized, telling you to fetch them before proceeding so reverse-engineering can read the code.
* `/aidlc --doctor` gains an advisory `Submodules:` row: no `.gitmodules`, all initialized, uninitialized (names the count, the paths, and the remedy), or present-but-unparseable. Advisory only - it never flips doctor's exit code.
* The read-only `detect` utility gains a `submodules` key in its `--json` payload and a `Submodules:` line in its human output when submodules are present.

# aidlc-workflows 2.2.3

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.2.3] - 2026-07-05

Fixes a fragile process respawn in the Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, and Codex hook adapters. Each adapter dispatches the framework's core lifecycle hooks (and, on Kiro, the off-band utility commands) by spawning a child process named `bun` by bare name. That child inherits the hook environment's `$PATH`, which on GUI-launched apps and minimal server environments often omits the bun install dir (`~/.bun/bin`), so the spawn fails with `Executable not found in $PATH: bun` and the whole hook layer dies. The adapters now respawn via the absolute path of the bun binary already running them (`process.execPath`), so the hooks themselves run again without `bun` on `PATH`: audit logging, session lifecycle, state validation, and subagent tracking are fully restored. Known limitation: four core hooks spawn a further `bun` child of their own (the stop guard's engine consult, the statusline state sync, the runtime-graph compile, and the sensor dispatch), and those children still resolve `bun` off `PATH`, so on a `bun`-less `PATH` they stay degraded (the stop guard fails open, the statusline does not update, the runtime graph is not recompiled, sensors do not fire); a follow-up threads the running binary down to those spawns. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* Kiro CLI, Kiro IDE, and Codex hook adapters no longer fail with `Executable not found in $PATH: "bun"` when the hook environment lacks the bun install dir; they reuse the exact bun binary running the adapter instead of resolving `bun` off `PATH`.
* Known limitation when `bun` is not on the hook environment's `PATH`: the stop guard, statusline sync, runtime-graph compile, and sensor dispatch respawn `bun` by bare name one level deeper and remain degraded there; the other lifecycle hooks are fully restored.
* No new commands or flags; no breaking change for CI or scripts.

* `bundle:` frontmatter renamed to `plugin:`. The old key is rejected everywhere it is read - schema validation errors with "bundle: was renamed; write plugin: for ownership", and the compose hook skips a contribution carrying it with a drop naming the same fix. The word is reserved for a possible future collection-of-plugins concept and is otherwise unused.

Plugin scope files are `<plugin>-<name>.md`, agent files `<plugin>-<role>-agent.md`. A plugin's `memory/` tree stays deferred. Three compose guards protect the install: composing onto an engine whose schema predates the `plugin:` key skips the plugin-owned content with a degraded drop naming the remediation (re-copy the shell, re-run compose) instead of permanently breaking the install's compile; every plugin stage file is validated against the INSTALLED engine's schema before it lands - an invalid one (e.g. a stale tree still authoring `bundle:`, or a frontmatter-only empty body) is skip-and-dropped naming the file and errors instead of bricking every later graph compile of the whole install; and a plugin file whose frontmatter `name:` collides with an installed agent/scope (even under a different filename) is skipped with a drop naming both files instead of bricking the loaders. Invariants: a plugin-owned slug must start with `<plugin>-`; `plugin: aidlc` is rejected; plugin names must not start with `aidlc-` (reserved for core - an `aidlc-<x>` plugin's runner dirs would land on core runner paths and clobber them; enforced at compile, compose, scope loading, and the packager); a stage file's name stem must match its slug; duplicate scope names and agent slugs across files fail loudly naming both files.

The scope-runner default batch is now data (`runner: true` scope frontmatter), not a code constant. The compose hook regenerates runners and the SKILL.md generated tables after recompile, so composed stages are typeable and visible immediately. Generated runners carry a `generated-by: aidlc-runner-gen` frontmatter marker and pruning requires it - a user-authored skill that quotes the runner commands is left alone and listed on stderr as unmanaged (pre-marker generated runners are still pruned by their exact generated dir name for one release). An empty scope batch only prunes under an active selection; otherwise it warns and preserves runners.
* New `select-plugins <name>[,<name>...]` utility verb: validates names, writes the selection to `tools/data/harness.json`, recompiles, and regenerates every generated surface in one transactional step (snapshot + rollback on failure - no torn installs). Stage numbers are selection-stable. A closure guard fails a selection that leaves an enabled stage consuming a required artifact whose only producers are disabled, naming the plugin to enable. `/aidlc --doctor` reports the selection and hard-fails on selection/graph disagreement (a stage file whose frontmatter cannot be parsed counts as missing under an active selection, with the parse error in the fix message). Composed scopes (authored by the adaptive composer at runtime) survive any selection unconditionally - grid entry, scope file, and runner all round-trip intact through deselect/re-enable. Each successful selection change emits a `PLUGIN_SELECTION_CHANGED` audit event recording the previous and new selection. On installs without a harness `skills/` dir (Codex) the runner regeneration steps are skipped with a note instead of erroring.
* Disabling a plugin removes what it merged, not just its own files: compose records the structural adds it actually applied to core stages in a per-plugin sidecar (`tools/data/plugin-contrib-<key>.json`), and `select-plugins` strips a disabled plugin's merged produces/sensors/consumes/required_sections (via the sidecar) and spliced prose (via the fragment sentinels) from installed stage source, inside the same rollback transaction. Re-enabling restores everything on the next session start (the plugin's compose hook re-merges byte-identically). Compose no longer merges contributions for a plugin the current selection disables (its stage/scope/agent copies still land - those are runtime-filtered).
* `select-plugins` refuses a change that would strand an active workflow: disabling the plugin that owns a running workflow's scope, or one owning a pending EXECUTE stage in its plan, is rejected naming each dependency and the remediation (complete or park the workflow, or keep the plugin enabled). `/aidlc --doctor` gains a matching hard-fail row for a selection that already strands one, plus an advisory listing `requires_stage` ordering edges the selection silently drops (an enabled stage requiring a disabled one - legitimate in plugin-only installs, but now explainable).
* The SKILL.md Stage Graph table is now generator output (`stage-table` verb, BEGIN/END markers, `--check` drift guard), and `state-template.md` documents the state-file contract instead of hand-enumerating stages - both surfaces follow the filtered graph under a selection. The scope-table BEGIN marker now uses a hyphen (matching the stage-table grammar); installed SKILL.md copies refresh on the next compose, and a stale-marker install degrades to an advisory drop, not an error.
* The walking-skeleton ceremony reads a new `skeleton: on|off` scope frontmatter field instead of a hardcoded core-scope name set, so plugin scopes are first-class in the ceremony. `AWS_AIDLC_DEFAULT_SCOPE` naming a disabled scope now falls back to the sole enabled plugin's first scope instead of dying, so a plugin-only install starts from plain `/aidlc` - and the substitution is announced on stderr naming both scopes instead of happening silently.
* Plugin stages must have a non-empty body after the frontmatter fence - a frontmatter-only stage compiles and routes while being behaviorally dead; it fails the plugin content tests, and the compose stage-file precheck skip-and-drops it at install time.
* Breaking for CI/scripts: none.

# aidlc-workflows 2.4.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.4.0] - 2026-07-14

Reviewers are now verifiers: every declared review runs under an explicit **adversarial review contract**. The reviewer's job is to refute the artifact, not confirm it - it assumes defects exist and hunts for them, and READY is the verdict it fails to reach after trying to break the artifact, not the default it starts from. Findings must ground in machine-checkable evidence where it exists: the reviewer runs the validation tools its invocation lists (via shell) and checks the artifact against its acceptance criteria, its stage definition, and the consumed upstream contracts; a finding backed only by opinion is a suggestion, not grounds for NOT-READY. This is a prompt-only release - the contract is written once into stage-protocol §12a (so any future reviewer inherits it) with short domain-voiced restatements in the two reviewer personas; no new tools, schema fields, or agents. Two scope decisions are on record: "validate deterministically" is read as grounding in machine-checkable evidence that already exists (validation tools, tests, acceptance criteria, contracts), not as building new domain validators; and the self-healing budget requirement is read as iterations OR tokens, satisfied by the existing `reviewer_max_iterations` (default 2) with human escalation at exhaustion - no token budget is added. The other two verifier properties were already in place: reviewers project a different model class than producers by default (2.3.1 tiers), and budget exhaustion already escalates to the human with full context. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project.

* Stage-protocol §12a step 2 now opens with the adversarial review contract: refute-don't-confirm posture, and evidence-grounding rules for findings. It applies to every stage that declares a `reviewer`, on all harnesses.
* Both reviewer personas restate the contract in their own domain voice - the Product Lead hunts untestable acceptance criteria, uncovered requirements, and orphan stories; the Architecture Reviewer hunts broken references, circular dependencies, and cross-unit claims the passed contracts do not back. Identity-marker and read-scope contracts are unchanged.
* The four harness orchestrator skills' reviewer steps carry a one-line restatement of the adversarial framing, following the read-scope precedent.
* No behavior change to the review loop mechanics: verdict flow, `reviewer_max_iterations`, HITL escalation, dispatch records, and the read-scope hook are all as in 2.3.4.

# aidlc-workflows 2.5.0

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.5.0] - 2026-07-17

The three-role ensemble (North Star Goal 1): a stage's `mode` is now its communication topology - who talks to whom while the body runs - and support agents become real, independently dispatched collaborators instead of voices the conductor adopts. Two new modes join `inline` and `subagent`: `pipeline` (chain: the links collectively author the artifacts in declared order, each seeing all upstream work; the final link leaves them complete) and `mob` (mesh as bounded rounds: all support agents contribute in parallel against the lead's draft, mutually blind; unresolved objections are triaged - judgment calls surface to the human mid-stage, knowledge disputes get one confirm-or-maintain round; maintained dissent is quoted verbatim at the approval gate). `mode: subagent` is strengthened to hub-and-spoke: on a stage with `support_agents`, each support agent is dispatched as a mutually-blind spoke against the lead's draft and the lead integrates. The writing model mirrors a real working session - everyone writes their own work: each dispatched collaborator writes a contribution file (`<stage>/contributions/<agent-slug>.md`, identity-marker first line, Contribution + Positions) and the lead alone edits the stage's `produces[]` artifacts. Those files double as deterministic completion evidence: the engine refuses approving a mob (or subagent-with-supports) stage while a declared collaborator's contribution file is missing. The conductor is the bus on every topology (only it delegates), and the reviewer loop is unchanged - a NOT-READY re-invokes the lead alone. `practices-discovery` ships as the hub-and-spoke showcase on greenfield and brownfield work (Pipeline & Deploy lead draft, mutually blind Quality + Developer + DevSecOps spokes, human interview, lead integration); `user-stories` ships as the mob showcase (Product Manager lead, Design + Developer + Quality collaborators, Product Lead reviewer). The shipped topology is 28 inline / 2 subagent / 1 pipeline / 1 mob. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project; on Kiro CLI/IDE also re-copy `.kiro/agents/` (nine new delegation-target agent configs plus an updated conductor `trustedAgents` list).

* New stage modes `pipeline` and `mob` (stage frontmatter + run-stage directive). Both require a non-empty `support_agents` - the compile rejects a chain with no links or a one-occupant room. `agent-team` stays reserved.
* Collaborator contribution files: dispatched support agents write `contributions/<agent-slug>.md` under the stage's record dir (first line `**Collaborator:** <agent-slug>` verbatim). `report --result approved` on an ensemble stage errors while one is missing or malformed, naming the gap and the fix; per-unit evidence follows only units the stage actually executes, and a no-DAG single iteration checks the ordinary stage directory. `AIDLC_DISABLE_ENSEMBLE_EVIDENCE=1` is the recovery escape hatch.
* Mob objection triage puts the human in the room: a judgment-call objection (both positions legitimate - scope, risk appetite, priority tradeoffs) surfaces mid-stage as a structured question; only knowledge disputes go to round 2. Under autonomous Construction the mid-stage turn is skipped - dissent is recorded and surfaces at the final-batch gate; it never halts the run.
* `reverse-engineering` re-modes from `subagent` to `pipeline`, recognizing the shape its body always had (developer scans, architect synthesizes and writes - a 2-link chain). No behavior change; the mode now tells the truth.
* `user-stories` flips to `mode: mob` and gains `aidlc-developer-agent` + `aidlc-quality-agent` as collaborators alongside `aidlc-design-agent`. Expect 3-6 additional bounded sub-agent dispatches on scopes that run it; each rides the collaborator's projected tier and the `tier_cap` clamp.
* `practices-discovery` flips to `mode: subagent` for both greenfield and brownfield runs: the Pipeline & Deploy lead drafts first, Quality + Developer + DevSecOps inspect it as mutually blind spokes, the human interview resolves gaps and judgment, and the lead integrates. Resume dispatches only missing spokes, and approval remains open until promotion into `aidlc/spaces/<active-space>/memory/{team,project}.md` succeeds.
* Stage lifecycle outcomes are report-owned: conductors report approval, rejection, revision, completion, or an explicit `skipped` result through `aidlc-orchestrate.ts`; the engine performs the atomic state/audit transition and routes onward. Direct `aidlc-state.ts` lifecycle mutations now fail with an engine-ownership error, so scripts must migrate those calls to `aidlc-orchestrate.ts report` (or the corresponding engine routing command). The PreToolUse redirect fires on Claude Code, Kiro CLI, Codex, and opencode (Kiro IDE relies on the CLI-level error - its hook payloads omit tool arguments). The adaptive composer now estimates implementation entropy before composing. ## [2.5.34] - 2026-08-03

The plugin contribution seam now merges `adds.scopes`: a plugin can put an existing core stage under one of its OWN scopes, so a single plugin scope can carry a run through both the plugin's stages and the core stages it routes onto. Previously the surface was declared-but-deferred (drop-logged, never merged). **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell and re-install/re-sync your plugins so the updated compose hook and `select-plugins` strip are in place; already-installed plugins recompose automatically on the next session start.

* Two guard rails, both dropped-with-log (visible in `/aidlc --doctor`), never merged: the scope's `scopes/<name>.md` identity file must already be installed, and that file's `plugin:` frontmatter must name the contributing plugin exactly (ownership is read from the installed file, never inferred from a name prefix; core scopes declare no `plugin:` and never merge).
* `/aidlc --select-plugins` now strips merged scope memberships when a plugin is disabled (recorded in the per-plugin contribution sidecar); re-enabling and recomposing restores them.
* Plugin compose hooks and `/aidlc --select-plugins` now share one workspace lock across stage mutations, contribution sidecars, selection changes, graph compilation, and rollback. Compose, plugin selection, intent birth, and in-flight recompose all queue for up to about 60 seconds behind live compose work, so concurrent plugin hooks cannot lose or skip each other's merges, disabling a plugin cannot race with compose and leave an untracked contribution active, and workflow mutations do not time out behind a legitimate compose.
* Workspace lock identity now resolves filesystem aliases, so the physical project path and a symlink to it cannot acquire separate compose/selection locks. Plugin identity comes from the host manifest (not plugin-authored stage/scope/contribution fields), mismatched ownership is dropped-with-log, and duplicate incoming scope identities are rejected before they can poison the installed roster.
* Quoted `adds.scopes` values participate in the same canonical set union as unquoted values. Disable removes only the membership compose actually added, preserving equivalent authored entries, and a failed graph compile rolls back newly copied plugin files and contribution writes so a corrected retry is not blocked by no-clobber.
* `adds.requires_stage` remains deferred (declared entries are still drop-logged, not merged).
* Graph compile now seeds NEW stage numbers in dependency order: each phase's batch of new stages is ordered by its own `requires_stage` edges before next-free indices are assigned (ties break by the authored `number:` hint, then slug; a cycle among new stages is a compile error). The engine owns all number values - a plugin's authored `number:` is a relative-ordering hint, never an absolute claim - so a multi-stage plugin's flow seeds validly regardless of filenames and uncoordinated plugins cannot collide on numbers. Already-pinned rows keep their JSON values unchanged; authored `name:` seeds the display name.

## [2.5.36] - 2026-08-03

Adds an optional declared workspace manifest for multi-repo teams. AI-DLC already auto-discovers sibling code repos on disk at intent birth; this release lets a team also declare that expected set in a `repos.json` file at the workspace root and reconcile it with a new `aidlc-workspace-sync` tool that clones missing repos, maintains a managed `.gitignore` block, and generates a VSCode multi-root workspace. The manifest is a convenience layer only: disk discovery remains the runtime source of truth, so a repo works the moment it is cloned whether or not it is declared. `--doctor` gains three advisory rows about manifest state. **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell to pick up the new tool; without `repos.json`, sync stays dormant and doctor adds only the advisory workspace-records row.

* New tool `aidlc-workspace-sync.ts` (run `bun <harness-dir>/tools/aidlc-workspace-sync.ts [--force]`): reads an optional `repos.json` (`{ "org", "repos": [{ "name", "branch"?, "url"? }] }`) at the workspace root, clones declared-but-missing repos on their declared branch, rewrites the managed block in the workspace `.gitignore`, and writes `aidlc.code-workspace`. Reconciles serialize under a workspace lock that cannot be reaped while its owner is alive; clones and generated files are staged before a reversible transaction. Concurrent manifest or output edits abort instead of applying stale state, no-replace installs close the final path race, and prior generated files are retained for recovery. Exit `0` in sync, `1` blocked/error with live paths unchanged, `2` synced with advisory warnings.
* Orphan safety: a checkout on disk but not in `repos.json` leaves the active sibling set only with `--force` after the tool overrides configurable status defaults, checks untracked and ignored content (including empty directories), hidden index state, stashes, refs and reflogs, unreachable Git objects, linked worktrees, submodules, and LFS object stores. Matching live refs must have fetchable object graphs - an advertised OID alone is not recovery proof - and local remotes whose storage or object alternates depend on the checkout cannot authorize removal. After revalidation, the checkout moves into transaction quarantine and receives the full local and live-remote proof again; its quarantined copy is retained in an ignored `.aidlc-workspace-sync-recovery-*` directory instead of being recursively deleted, so even a concurrent writer holding the directory open cannot lose a late write. Inspect and manually delete retained recovery copies when no longer needed. Existing repos are never re-cloned or branch-switched; their `branch` mismatch is advisory.
* `/aidlc --doctor` gains three advisory rows (they never change the exit code): uncommitted changes under `aidlc/`, `repos.json` vs on-disk sibling drift, and a stale managed `.gitignore` block. Doctor and sync share the same strict manifest schema, including safe immediate-child names, so invalid JSON or schema never appears synchronized. The drift and gitignore rows appear only when a `repos.json` exists, so single-repo installs do not gain manifest-specific rows.
* User Guide documents the optional manifest in Spaces and Intents and the tool invocation in CLI Commands, both stressing that the manifest never overrides runtime disk discovery.

## [2.5.43] - 2026-08-06

Stops `/aidlc --doctor` from reporting hook decay on the Kiro IDE harness when a write simply failed. The adapter recorded a visible hook drop whenever it could not extract a file path from a write tool's result, which conflated two very different situations: a write that FAILED (no artifact exists, so declining to forward it is correct) and a write that SUCCEEDED but whose result wording could not be parsed (the genuine degradation the drop log exists to surface). A failed `str_replace` - for example one whose old string matched multiple times - is no longer counted as a drop. The IDE 1.x stdin channel carries no success flag, so these failures arrive only as error prose and the existing `toolSuccess` guard could not catch them; every one of them was logged as decay, which trains the reader to ignore the one channel that matters when something genuinely breaks.

A match can only suppress a drop after path extraction has already failed and structured success is unavailable, and no known success wording begins with error prose, so the risk direction is one-way.

# aidlc-workflows 2.5.44

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.5.44] - 2026-08-06

Human-readable AI-DLC artifacts now follow the conversation language instead of defaulting to English. The framework rule layer gains four `## Mandated` rules in `org.md` that define how the conversation language is resolved, why it stays stable across short turns like `Approve`, which artifacts are localized, and which protocol tokens stay English. The rules travel to delegated agents and reviewers inside the active-stage rule bundle the dispatch-rules hook already delivers, so a subagent that never sees the conversation can still resolve the language from the rule layer, `aidlc-state.md`, or the upstream artifacts it consumes. **Upgrade:** fresh installs receive the rules with their seeded `default` space. An existing workspace keeps its own memory tree — runtime self-healing intentionally does not overwrite one — so merge the four rules into each `aidlc/spaces/<space>/memory/org.md` by hand and start a fresh session for them to load.

* Human-readable artifacts (requirements, user stories, plans, specs, reviews, questions, discovered practices, affirmed rules, evidence, decision rationale) are written in the workflow's established conversation language, including the descriptive text of a rule shaped as `ALWAYS …` / `NEVER …`.
* The conversation language is resolved in a fixed order — the `Conversation language:` line the orchestrator is now required to state in every delegated brief, then an explicit language rule in `project.md` — the only file a language switch is ever persisted to, and one that always outranks a `team.md` default, because the runtime rule chain concatenates `org → team → project → phase` and so bundle position is not recency: a newer team-level rule reaches an agent *before* a staler project-level one, and the winner is the stated precedence rather than the later position — then the verbatim `**Project**` description in `aidlc-state.md`, then any artifact or draft the agent was handed (the directive's `consumes[]` contracts, the artifact under review, or the lead draft it was dispatched against). The brief line ranks first because the orchestrator regenerates it from the live conversation on every dispatch, so it can never be staler than a rule already on disk. It is also mandatory because the file-reading sources can all be empty: a greenfield run of a stage whose `consumes` are every one `conditional_on: brownfield` reaches its dispatched lead with no upstream artifact at all.
* The language is stable: a turn carrying no language signal (`Approve`, `Looks correct`, an option letter or number, pasted code, a quoted error or stack trace, a bare path) never switches it. Only an explicit human request does, and that switch takes effect immediately — the orchestrator carries the new language in every subsequent brief. Recording it under `## Corrections` in `project.md` (never `team.md`) is durability, not activation, so nothing waits on the human-gated learnings ritual — and that ritual is the only sanctioned write path for persisting a language switch, so agents never hand-edit a memory file to record one, while the deterministic memory writers a stage invokes by contract (such as `aidlc-state.ts practices-promote`) are unaffected. A declined persistence is a correct outcome: the brief carries the language for the rest of the session. A persisted rule never outranks the brief or a later explicit switch request — it is the fallback for a brief that states no language — and because the learnings write path appends rather than replaces, the last conversation-language rule under `## Corrections` in `project.md` is the current one.
* That stability guarantee is scoped to the session, which is as far as the brief line can carry an unpersisted switch. A workflow outlives a session, and the resume context injected at session start carries scope, phase, stage, status, agent and next action but no language, so the first turn of a new session re-resolves the language before dispatching anything: the persisted rule, else the human-readable artifacts the workflow has already produced, else the verbatim initial description — and it asks the human rather than defaulting to English when all of those are silent. Re-resolving is not a switch, and is never announced or persisted as one. Accepting the learnings ritual is therefore what makes a switch survive a resume.
* The English exception is now scoped to machine-parsed syntax rather than whole files, and states a general principle: a literal a stage file spells in backticks and tells you to write exactly is a fixed token — including option labels and sentinel values, not just syntax. Named instances cover `[Answer]:` tags and the mandatory `X. Other (please specify)` option, the `A. Accept assumptions` / `B. Convert to follow-up questions` confirmation answers the engine compares literally, the `None.`/`None` sentinels, `AGREE:`/`OBJECT:` prefixes, the `**Collaborator:** <agent-slug>` first line the engine matches exactly on a contribution file, the `[desc]`/`[scope]`/`[assumption]`/`[Q<n>]`/`[memory:M<n>]` source-register tags, template H2 headings the sensors match verbatim, the `READY`/`NOT-READY` verdicts, fenced YAML keys and enums, `aidlc-state.md` and audit-shard field labels, stable IDs, code, paths, mermaid keywords, and cross-references. Glossing a literal when presenting it to a human is allowed; what is written into an artifact is the literal. Prose surrounding a preserved token is localized, and a Markdown artifact is no longer treated as English just because a tool parses part of it.

# aidlc-workflows 2.5.54

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.5.54] - 2026-08-07

Stage reviews now run under a review class, cutting the dominant latency cost of the human-gated prose stages. Live A/B runs against the real harness showed the adversarial refute-fix-re-review loop spending 12+ minutes per inception stage on review choreography alone (the shape behind reports of 30-minute Requirements Analysis waits); the 7 human-gated ideation/inception prose stages now default to a single advisory pass whose findings are quoted verbatim at the approval gate for the human to triage, while the 5 Construction design/build stages keep the full adversarial loop. The iteration cap is now engine-enforced rather than prose-only, and the reviewer tier runs at medium effort (measured at ~half the review wall-clock with no finding-quality loss). **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` shell into the project; existing workflows pick the classes up on the next stage directive.

* New stage frontmatter field `review_class: adversarial | advisory` (requires `reviewer`; defaults to `adversarial` when a reviewer is declared). The 7 prose stages (intent-capture, rough-mockups, requirements-analysis, user-stories, refined-mockups, application-design, units-generation) ship `advisory`; the 5 Construction stages (functional-design, nfr-requirements, nfr-design, infrastructure-design, code-generation) stay `adversarial`.
* Advisory contract: one review pass, both verdicts terminal, `reviewer_max_iterations` pinned to 1, findings ranked by severity and quoted verbatim at the approval gate; a Request Changes at the gate is how a finding becomes a revision. Evidence-grounding still applies; the reviewer personas carry the advisory stance.
* Scope ceiling: scopes may declare `review_cap: adversarial | advisory | none`; the shipped `bugfix`, `poc`, and `workshop` scopes cap to `advisory`. Invalid values fail scope metadata loading loudly.
* New per-run override `/aidlc --review <adversarial|advisory|none>`: lowers the effective class for the active workflow (low-wins against stage declaration and scope cap; `adversarial` clears the override and can never raise a class). Birth, flat-layout migration, scope-change, and same-scope config routes all preserve it; a missing value is rejected instead of silently retaining the prior policy; `none` removes both reviewer dispatch and the matching completion receipt requirement outside autonomous Bolts. Updates the `Review Override` state field, emits the new `REVIEW_CLASS_CHANGED` audit event (78-event taxonomy), and shows in `config list` / `config get review`.
* Engine-enforced iteration ceiling: `aidlc-log.ts review` requires a positive `--iteration`, derives the next ordinal from current-attempt audit history under the audit lock, and refuses duplicate, out-of-order, or over-budget `REVIEW_REQUESTED` rows (advisory 1, adversarial `reviewer_max_iterations`, override `none` 0). A failed or interrupted dispatch can explicitly reuse its unmatched request with `--retry-pending`; the retry is audit-marked and consumes no new iteration. Inline per-unit stages keep scope/run caps; only a matching autonomous Bolt attempt uses the declared class. `REVIEW_COMPLETED` receipts remain recordable after dispatch, and both review events are reserved from every public `aidlc-audit` append route.
* Autonomous swarm (Bolt) reviews are exempt from scope caps and run overrides: inside a Bolt the reviewer is the only pre-merge verification, so the declared class always applies, including advisory's single-pass limit.
* The reviewer tier (`balanced`: product-lead + architecture-reviewer) now pins `medium` reasoning effort on Claude, Codex, and opencode instead of inheriting the session effort.

# aidlc-workflows 2.5.55

[All releases / 更新履歴一覧](../changelog.md) · [改善点の日本語ガイド](../release-highlights.md)

## [2.5.55] - 2026-08-07

Hardens the human-authorization boundary and adds unit-of-work lifecycle receipts, closing the reliability and authorization gaps reported in the brownfield Codex evaluation (issue 681). **Upgrade:** re-copy your `dist/<harness>/` tree into the project; if your CI drives gates against bare fixtures via the audit CLI, set `AIDLC_ALLOW_DIRECT_AUDIT_EVENTS=1` in those runs (the test suite sets it automatically).

* The public audit CLI is now a diagnostic escape hatch only: `aidlc-audit.ts append` / `append-batch` refuse authority-bearing receipts (`HUMAN_TURN`, `GATE_APPROVED`, `GATE_REJECTED`, `QUESTION_ANSWERED`, `REVIEW_REQUESTED`, `REVIEW_COMPLETED`, `SWARM_STARTED`, `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED`, `AUTONOMY_MODE_SET`, and the four `UNIT_*` lifecycle receipts) with an error naming the owning tool; `append-raw` refuses taxonomy `**Event**:` lines and line-breaking headings; audit field names use a strict single-line label grammar, closing control-character injection as well as the exact `Event` key.
* `aidlc-bolt.ts set-autonomy --mode autonomous` requires a fresh human turn (the ladder-prompt answer), and one audit lock now covers the presence check, receipt, and state write so concurrent grants consume that turn exactly once; switching back to `gated` needs no presence. The error tells the conductor to ask the human to confirm autonomy in a typed message.
* Human-presence freshness is now shard-aware: a candidate human turn must be provably newer than every latest resolution; when any resolution shares its second-precision timestamp in another audit shard, the gate fails closed and asks for a fresh turn instead of trusting shard filename order.
* Cancellation boilerplate ("Cancelled", "dismissed", "timed out", empty text) is refused as an interview answer (`aidlc-log.ts answer`), an approval choice (`approve --user-input`), and rejection feedback (`reject --feedback`) — a dismissed question widget can no longer mint a `QUESTION_ANSWERED` or commit a gate. A substantive rejection now also requires and consumes a fresh human turn, matching approval.
* New unit-of-work lifecycle receipts on inline per-unit Construction stages: `aidlc-state.ts unit start|pause|resume|complete` emits `UNIT_STARTED` / `UNIT_PAUSED` / `UNIT_RESUMED` / `UNIT_COMPLETED` (event taxonomy 78 → 82). `unit start` accepts safe legacy DAG names, including digit-leading names such as `2fa`, but must match the engine's exact routed stage/Unit pair, so dependencies and earlier same-batch Units cannot be bypassed. Autonomous swarms preserve those legacy Unit identities while deriving deterministic, collision-resistant internal Bolt slugs for worktree operations. A retained autonomy grant no longer blocks receipts after a backward jump to an inline stage; swarm-owned stages still refuse interactive receipts. State-mirrored checkpoint text stays on one line, and every receipt carries an exact stage-attempt `Run floor`; unit-major receipts survive their stage's later start, while workflow/jump/rejection boundaries invalidate them. Cross-shard same-second boundary ambiguity invalidates prior receipts instead of trusting shard filename order, and lifecycle ties preserve a possible pause or other non-terminal state instead of settling or resuming the unit. Receipt mode remains active across attempts, so stale rows cannot restore artifact-only settlement. `unit complete` requires regular artifact files; directories named `*.md` do not count. Once any receipt exists for a stage, the engine requires a receipt per unit.
* Swarm `prepare` now stamps successfully prepared worktrees with the exact stage attempt; failed re-prepares cannot relabel preserved worktrees. `finalize` refuses a stale prepared attempt before merge and carries the captured token into `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED`, closing same-second and late-retry convergence replay. In-flight worktrees prepared by the preceding unstamped release remain finalizable when their frozen fork evidence and hash prove they belong to the current attempt; stale or incomplete legacy preparations still fail closed.
* A paused unit hard-stops the engine: `next` emits an ask naming the unit, its recorded `--reason`, and `--next-action` (`unit_state: paused`) until an explicit `unit resume`, and `report --result awaiting-approval` is refused while a unit of the stage is paused. `unit start` refuses while another unit is open (one active unit at a time).
* The state file mirrors the active checkpoint under `## Runtime State` (`Active Unit`, `Unit State`, `Unit Pause Reason`, `Unit Next Action`) so `--status` and session resume land on the exact stopping point.
